font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>fewer, bigger</text></svg>
🎯 Take profit % and 🛑 stop loss %

Your default exits. Every practice buy pre-fills them (you can still override per trade). Example: 🎯 20 / 🛑 15 risks 15 to make 20 — a gap between them lets you be wrong more often than right and still come out ahead, IF you honour the stop. Leave BOTH at 0 and the 🪤 trailing stop below does the whole job on its own — which is what ⚡ Hunter does — favoured first by the 1 August 2026 testing and again by the 13 August 2026 ten-year replay, where the trailing exit's margin over fixed exits held across the whole decade.
📦 Max in one share

The concentration guardrail, as a % of your account. Auto-pilot sizes buys with it and TRIMS any buy that would breach it; manual buys over it show a friendly flag in your 🔔 briefing — never a block. You stay in charge; the rule stays visible.
🔢 Max open positions
More positions than you can genuinely follow is a blur, not a portfolio. Auto-pilot will not open a new position beyond this number. For most people 5–8 is plenty while learning.
🪤 Trailing stop — the stop that follows success

Set a % (say 8) and your stop follows the highest CLOSE since you bought, always that % below it — and it only ever moves UP. A share that runs 40% then rolls over gets sold 8% off its peak instead of riding all the way back down. 0 = off. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='10,70 50,62 90,66 130,50 170,54 210,38 250,42 300,30' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><polyline points='10,86 50,78 90,78 130,66 170,66 210,54 250,54 300,46' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 3'/><text x='14' y='20' fill='#4ade80' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>price makes new highs…</text><text x='120' y='96' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>…the trailing stop climbs behind it - and NEVER moves down</text><circle cx='300' cy='30' r='3.5' fill='#4ade80'/><circle cx='300' cy='46' r='3.5' fill='#f5c84c'/></svg>
🛡 Break-even — the free trade

At +X% gain (say 5), the stop jumps to your entry price. From that moment the worst realistic outcome is $0 lost — you're playing with the market's money, and letting a winner run suddenly feels easy. 0 = off. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='10' y1='48' x2='310' y2='48' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.4' stroke-dasharray='6 4'/><text x='14' y='42' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>your entry price</text><polyline points='10,60 60,56 110,50 160,40' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><text x='116' y='28' fill='#4ade80' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>+5%</text><line x1='10' y1='84' x2='160' y2='84' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 3'/><text x='14' y='80' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>old stop</text><line x1='170' y1='80' x2='170' y2='56' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='164,52 172,56 164,60' fill='#f5c84c'/><line x1='176' y1='48' x2='310' y2='48' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='2.4'/><text x='240' y='40' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>stop jumps to entry</text><text x='240' y='62' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>worst case from here: $0 lost</text><text x='240' y='74' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a free trade</text></svg>
⏱ Max hold — capital has a job

N data days after entry, an undecided position exits at the next open. Dead money in a going-nowhere trade has a cost: everything else it could have been doing. Day traders call this a time stop. 0 = off.
The human checklist + the ON/OFF switch

The free-text box is for rules numbers can't hold: 'Never average down. Wait for a green day. Review Sundays.' And the whole panel has an ON/OFF toggle — some people want the app silent about rules, and one tap is respected everywhere.

quiz.q: Your rules say 🎯 20% / 🛑 8%. What's the honest way to describe that trade?
a: Risking 8 to make 20 — profitable over time even winning only half your trades, IF the stop is honoured
quiz.why: Risk:reward asymmetry is the engine. Five wins (+100) against five losses (−40) is +60 per ten trades at only a 50% hit rate.

quiz.q: You buy at $10.00 with a 🪤 trailing stop of 8%. The highest close reaches $15.00, then the share slides. Where is your stop?
a: $13.80 — 8% below the $15 peak close; it followed the rise and never moves down
quiz.why: The trail ratchets: each new highest close lifts the stop to peak × 0.92. Rises are followed, falls are not — that's how winners get protected.

quiz.q: What does 🛡 break-even at +5% actually change?
a: Once a close is 5% above your entry, the stop moves UP to your entry — the trade can no longer realistically become a loss
quiz.why: It converts open risk into a 'free trade'. Full upside stays; the realistic downside becomes zero (a brutal overnight gap can still pierce it).

quiz.q: Why use a ⏱ time stop when the share has hit neither 🎯 nor 🛑?
a: Flat, going-nowhere capital has an invisible cost — the trades it CAN'T take. If the idea hasn't worked in N days, the reason you bought is probably stale
quiz.why: An entry thesis has a shelf life. Recycling stuck capital into fresh setups is a professional habit — and it caps how long a slow bleed can run.

title: 12 · Auto-pilot I — your rules, on autopilot
steps: What Auto-pilot is

A practice-money robot that applies YOUR saved rules to each fresh day of data — once per day, hands-off. It finds candidates the way you would (scans + filters), sizes buys by your 📦 rule, sets your 🎯/🛑 automatically, and writes every decision in a diary. It's the discipline of your rules without the temptation of your moods. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 104' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='34' width='84' height='36' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='52' y='50' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>fresh day</text><text x='52' y='62' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>of data</text><line x1='94' y1='52' x2='126' y2='52' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='120,48 128,52 120,56' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='130' y='34' width='84' height='36' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='172' y='50' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>YOUR rules</text><text x='172' y='62' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>applied</text><line x1='214' y1='52' x2='246' y2='52' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='240,48 248,52 240,56' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='250' y='20' width='62' height='28' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='281' y='38' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>buy</text><rect x='250' y='56' width='62' height='28' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='281' y='74' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>skip</text><text x='160' y='94' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>once per day, hands off - and every decision lands in the diary</text></svg>
What it can NEVER do

Auto-pilot trades the PRACTICE account only. It cannot touch a real broker, move real money, or place real orders — there is no code path to do so. Think flight simulator: the whole point is to prove (or disprove) your rules where mistakes are free.
Switching on

📐 My Rules → 🤖 Auto-pilot → ON — or just tap a preset, which saves the rules and switches the bot on in one go. It's OFF by default and stays off until YOU choose. Once per fresh data day; opening the app twice doesn't buy twice. And the rules travel now: every save with the bot ON quietly mirrors your bot numbers to YOUR server, which decides picks with them at the end of every trading day — even on days the app never opens. Your next open places those decisions as practice orders dated the day they were made, and the fills replay honestly from each decision day.
The two lanes

Lane 1 — the SCANNER: picks candidates from a scan you choose and buys the best by your criteria. Lane 2 — 🎯 MY PICKS: shares YOU chose at YOUR exact prices (next lesson). Picks run first; the scanner then works with whatever cash and position slots remain. A third source now sits above both: 🌐 SERVER DECISIONS — picks your own saved rules chose on the server at end-of-day, placed first as dated practice orders when you next open. On a day the server has decided, the local scanner stands down, so the bot never decides one day twice. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='14' width='146' height='66' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='83' y='30' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Lane 1 - SCANNER</text><text x='83' y='46' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>picks candidates from</text><text x='83' y='57' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a scan you choose,</text><text x='83' y='68' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>best-first by your rules</text><rect x='164' y='14' width='146' height='66' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='237' y='30' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Lane 2 - MY PICKS</text><text x='237' y='46' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>shares YOU chose</text><text x='237' y='57' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>at YOUR exact price,</text><text x='237' y='68' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>watched every day</text></svg>
Scanner settings, one by one

Buy from: 🧪 Best proven scan (auto — follows whichever lens your report card currently grades best), 🏆 Top 20 by Watch Score, or another lens (🔥 Unusual Activity, 🚨 Sharp Mover, 📈 Volume, ↩️ Recovery, 🫧 Quiet Movers, 🪜 Pullback). Buys per day: 1–3 max. Min Watch Score: e.g. 7 = only strong setups (0 = off). 🔇 quiet only: skip shares with likely recent news. Signal ticks (🚀 breakout · 🕵️ informed? · 🏦 inst? · ⤴ MA cross · 🧑‍💼 director ✓ · 🥇 vol record): require at least one ticked signal to be showing.
Sizing: 💵 $ per buy or 📦 %

Set a fixed practice-dollar amount per buy, or leave it blank to size by your 📦 max-per-share %. Either way 📦 is the guardrail: a buy that would breach it gets TRIMMED to fit, parcels under the $500 ASX minimum are skipped, and the 💧 liquidity floor keeps it out of shares that barely trade.
Every decision on the record

The diary logs each run: what it bought and WHY (which signals), and what it skipped and why — score too low, already held, would breach 📦, under $500, liquidity too thin, day-jump too big… Your 🔔 morning briefing lists any overnight buys. Nothing happens silently, ever.
The safety rails, all in one place

OFF by default · practice money only · once per fresh data day · buys-per-day capped · never doubles into a share it already holds or has on order · respects 🔢 max positions, 📦 sizing, 💧 liquidity and the $500 minimum · every action logged. Switch it off at any moment; nothing it did is hidden.
Its own $50k test account

Auto-pilot trades a SEPARATE practice account — opened with $50,000 — so the robot's results never mix with your own trading. Switch between 👤 My trading and 🤖 Auto-pilot with the tabs at the top of the 💼 Portfolio window. Buys you make from the table always go to YOUR account; sells and undo inside the 🤖 view act on the bot's account (so you can step in and close a bot position). The bot's 📦 sizing and 🔢 position limits are measured against ITS $50k, and the Scoreboard grades ITS account only — a clean experiment, exactly how a fund would trial a new strategy. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='16' y='14' width='130' height='68' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='81' y='32' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>👤 YOUR account</text><text x='81' y='50' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>your trades,</text><text x='81' y='64' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>your record</text><rect x='174' y='14' width='130' height='68' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='239' y='32' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>🤖 robot account</text><text x='239' y='50' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>its own $50,000</text><text x='239' y='64' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>practice money</text><line x1='146' y1='48' x2='174' y2='48' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='3 3'/><text x='160' y='90' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>results never mix - switch views any time</text></svg>

quiz.q: Auto-pilot is ON and you open the app three times on the same data day. How many times does it act?
a: Once — it runs per fresh data DAY, not per app open
quiz.why: The run is keyed to the data date. Re-opening the app on the same day's data does nothing — no accidental double-buying.

quiz.q: Can Auto-pilot place a real-money order?
a: No — it is wired to the practice account only; there is no real-broker code path. It's a flight simulator for your rules
Only if you enable it twice
quiz.why: Practice-only by design. Proving your rules with pretend money is the whole job; anything involving real money is a completely separate, human decision.

quiz.q: Your 📦 rule is 10% of a $10,000 account, and 💵 $ per buy is set to $1,500. What does Auto-pilot buy?
a: About $1,000 — the buy is TRIMMED to your 📦 cap; the guardrail always has the final say
quiz.why: 💵 sets the wish, 📦 sets the law. Conflicts resolve to the safer number, and the diary notes the trim.

quiz.q: Where do you find out why Auto-pilot did NOT buy anything today?
a: You can't — it's a black box
The diary — every skip is logged with its reason (score too low, would breach limits, nothing qualified…)
quiz.why: No-action days are recorded with reasons too. A robot you can audit is the only kind worth running.

title: 13 · Auto-pilot II — 🎯 My Picks & 🔁 repeat
steps: Your shares, your prices

The scanner hunts broadly; My Picks is the sniper lane. YOU name the share, the exact buy price, and (optionally) the exact sell 🎯 and stop 🛑. Auto-pilot places a practice LIMIT buy at your price and manages the exit — your plan, executed without you watching the screen. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='14' width='140' height='68' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='80' y='30' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>SCANNER lane</text><text x='80' y='46' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>casts a wide net -</text><text x='80' y='58' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>whatever qualifies</text><text x='80' y='70' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>today</text><rect x='170' y='14' width='140' height='68' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='240' y='30' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>MY PICKS lane</text><circle cx='240' cy='52' r='12' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='240' y1='36' x2='240' y2='44' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='240' y1='60' x2='240' y2='68' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='224' y1='52' x2='232' y2='52' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='248' y1='52' x2='256' y2='52' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='240' y='80' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>THIS share at THIS price</text></svg>
Setting one up

In 📐 My Rules under 🎯 My picks: Code (e.g. BHP), Buy at (your entry), Sell at (🎯), Stop (🛑), $ amount, and the 🔁 repeat tick. Leave sell/stop blank and your % rules fill them in. The pick sits as a pending practice limit order — filling only if the share actually trades down to your price.
Why a LIMIT order?
Because a pick means 'I want THIS share at THIS price' — not at any price. If it never dips to your level, you simply don't own it (and lost nothing). Patience is enforced by the order type itself.
One fill, then disarm

A normal pick disarms after it fills — it will never re-buy in a loop on its own. Your 🎯/🛑 manage the exit from there. Add a pick for a share you ALREADY hold and it applies your sell/stop to that holding instead of buying more.
🔁 Repeat — the cycle trade

Tick 🔁 and the pick becomes a cycle: buy at your price → sell at your 🎯 → re-arm → buy the dip again. Each completed cycle is counted ('cycle 2', 'cycle 3'…) in the diary. For a share that oscillates in a range you trust, this automates the round trip. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 104' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='38' width='84' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='62' y='52' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>buy the dip</text><text x='62' y='63' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>at YOUR price</text><line x1='104' y1='53' x2='136' y2='53' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='130,49 138,53 130,57' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='140' y='38' width='84' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='182' y='52' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>sell at your</text><text x='182' y='63' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>target</text><line x1='224' y1='53' x2='256' y2='53' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='250,49 258,53 250,57' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='260' y='38' width='50' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='285' y='57' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>re-arm</text><path d='M 285 68 L 285 88 L 62 88 L 62 68' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.3' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><polygon points='58,72 62,64 66,72' fill='#54627f'/><text x='160' y='14' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the cycle trade - each loop is one counted cycle</text></svg>
Why repeat PAUSES after a stop

If a cycle ends on the 🛑 — a loss — the repeat does NOT re-arm. A share that broke below your stop is telling you the range you trusted may be gone; re-buying automatically would churn losses. The pick shows ⏸ paused with the reason; re-arming is a deliberate human tap. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 88' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='14' y='30' width='90' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='59' y='44' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>cycle ends</text><text x='59' y='55' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>on the STOP</text><line x1='104' y1='45' x2='136' y2='45' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='130,41 138,45 130,49' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='140' y='30' width='90' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='185' y='44' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>repeat</text><text x='185' y='55' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>PAUSES</text><line x1='230' y1='45' x2='262' y2='45' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='256,41 264,45 256,49' fill='#8fa0c9'/><text x='288' y='42' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>you decide</text><text x='288' y='54' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>to re-add</text><text x='160' y='78' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a break below your stop says the range you trusted is broken</text></svg>
Picks share the same budget
Picks place first; the scanner then uses the cash and 🔢 position slots left over. Every guardrail — 📦 trim, $500 minimum, no doubling into held shares — applies to picks too.

quiz.q: Your pick: buy CSL at $27.50. It never trades below $29 all month. What happened?
a: Nothing — the limit order waits at YOUR price; no dip, no buy, no loss
The pick converts to a market order
quiz.why: A limit pick is a standing offer at your price only. Not filling is a feature — the plan was 'CSL at $27.50', not 'CSL at whatever'.

quiz.q: What does ticking 🔁 repeat change about a pick?
a: After it sells at your 🎯 it re-arms and buys your price again — cycling until you remove it (and pausing instead if a cycle ends on the 🛑)
It repeats the same buy every day
quiz.why: 🔁 automates buy-dip → sell-target → wait → repeat. One share, one cycle at a time, counted in the diary.

quiz.q: A 🔁 pick's latest cycle ended on the 🛑 stop. What does Auto-pilot do next?
a: Buys the dip again immediately — it's cheaper now
PAUSES the repeat and says why — a broken range shouldn't be re-bought on autopilot; restarting is your call
quiz.why: Stopping out means the market disagreed with the plan. The anti-churn pause stops a falling share draining you one stop-loss at a time.

quiz.q: You add a pick for a share you ALREADY hold. What happens?
a: It applies your sell 🎯 / stop 🛑 to the EXISTING holding — no double-up
quiz.why: Held shares don't get doubled into. The pick becomes exit management for the position you already have.

title: 14 · Auto-pilot III — exits that think
steps: Exits are where the money is

Anyone can buy. Profit is decided by the sell — and the sell is where emotions do the most damage (holding losers, snatching winners). The advanced exits automate the discipline: 🪤 trailing, 🛡 break-even, ⏱ time. Each is optional; 0 = off.
The fixed pair first
🎯 take-profit sells into strength at your %. 🛑 stop-loss caps the loss at your %. These are the seat-belts. The three below are upgrades that adapt to what the trade actually DOES.
🪤 Trailing stop — a walk-through

Buy $10.00, trail 8%. Day 1 closes $10.50 → stop rises to $9.66 (8% under the new peak close). Day 3 closes $12.00 → stop $11.04. The share then fades: the moment it touches $11.04 you're out — keeping most of the run instead of watching +20% become −5%. The stop NEVER moves down; a red day just leaves it parked. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 110' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='12' y='14' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>buy $10.00 - trail 8%</text><polyline points='14,72 62,60 110,66 158,44 206,50 254,28' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><text x='70' y='50' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>$10.50</text><text x='166' y='34' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>$12.00</text><path d='M 14 92 L 62 80 L 110 80 L 158 62 L 206 62 L 254 46 L 306 46' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='5 3'/><text x='70' y='92' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>$9.66</text><text x='166' y='74' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>$11.04</text><text x='160' y='106' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the stop steps UP under each new peak close - never down</text></svg>
🛡 Break-even — the free trade

At your set gain (say +5% on a close), the stop jumps to your entry. Now the trade can win big or scratch to zero — but barring a gap it can't lose. Psychologically, this is the setting that makes letting winners run bearable.
⏱ Time stop

If a position is still undecided after your max-hold data days, it exits at the next OPEN. Trends that never came; capital freed for the next setup. The history badge is ⏱, so you can always tell a time exit from a stop-out.
Gap honesty

End-of-day truth: if bad news gaps a share from $10 to $8.40 overnight and your stop was $9.20, you get $8.40 — the open — because that's the first price anyone could really sell at. The engine never pretends you got your stop in a crash, so your practice stats stay believable. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='14,34 70,30 126,36 182,32' fill='none' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='2.2'/><text x='100' y='22' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>$10 - going fine</text><line x1='14' y1='52' x2='182' y2='52' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.6' stroke-dasharray='6 4'/><text x='18' y='64' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>your stop $9.20</text><circle cx='182' cy='32' r='3' fill='#8fa0c9'/><line x1='196' y1='32' x2='224' y2='78' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='3 3'/><circle cx='224' cy='78' r='3.5' fill='#f87171'/><text x='232' y='82' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>opens $8.40 - you get $8.40</text><text x='160' y='97' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>overnight news gaps PAST your stop: the fill is the OPEN, honestly</text></svg>
Reading the exits afterwards

Every closed trade is badged by its trigger: 🎯 target · 🛑 stop · 🪤 trailing · ⏱ time. The stop history records each 🪤 ratchet step, so you can replay exactly how the stop climbed behind the price. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 92' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='12' y='14' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>every closed trade wears its exit badge:</text><rect x='12' y='22' width='140' height='16' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='20' y='33' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>CSL  +18.2%</text><text x='120' y='33' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>target</text><rect x='12' y='42' width='140' height='16' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='20' y='53' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>XYZ  -7.9%</text><text x='126' y='53' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>stop</text><rect x='12' y='62' width='140' height='16' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='20' y='73' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>BHP  +11.4%</text><text x='114' y='73' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>trailing</text><rect x='166' y='22' width='140' height='16' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='174' y='33' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>WOW  +0.8%</text><text x='276' y='33' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>time</text><text x='166' y='58' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>the pattern of your badges</text><text x='166' y='70' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>tells you which exit is doing</text><text x='166' y='82' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>the real work</text></svg>
Starter settings that behave

Two kits worth knowing. The cautious one: 🪤 trail 8%, 🛡 break-even at +5%, ⏱ max hold 10 days, with 🎯 20 / 🛑 15. The tested one: 🪤 trail 20% and NOTHING else — no take-profit, no fixed stop, no break-even, no time limit. The second looks reckless and measured far better over the stored history, because a take-profit sells the rare huge winner in its first week. Very tight trails (3–4%) get shaken out by normal daily noise. On the ten-year width test, 15% cut winners too early, 20% was the peak — the best surviving return and the shallowest fall — and 30% posted a bigger headline while doubling the drawdown and keeping less once its three best trades were removed. Tune against your own Scoreboard, not against one lucky trade.

quiz.q: Buy $10, trail 8%. Highest close so far $12. Today closes DOWN at $11.30. Where's the stop tonight?
a: Still $11.04 — 8% under the $12 peak; the trail never moves DOWN on a red day
quiz.why: The ratchet only turns one way. Down days leave the stop parked; only a NEW highest close lifts it.

quiz.q: Overnight news gaps a share from $10.00 straight down to $8.40. Your 🛑 was $9.20. The practice account sells at…
a: $8.40 — the open; the market never traded at $9.20, and pretending otherwise would fake your stats
quiz.why: A stop is an instruction, not a guarantee. When price gaps through it, the first real exit is the open — the engine models the world as it is.

quiz.q: What's the practical effect of 🛡 break-even arming at +5%?
a: Your worst realistic outcome becomes $0 lost — the stop sits at your entry while the upside stays fully open
quiz.why: Break-even converts risk to zero without capping the win — the 'free trade'. (A brutal gap can still pierce it; gap honesty applies.)

quiz.q: Why does a ⏱ time exit fill at the next OPEN rather than that day's close?
a: Because the 'time is up' decision is made on tonight's data — the next genuine chance to sell is tomorrow's open. Same honesty as every other fill
quiz.why: All fills follow one rule: the first price a real person could actually have traded after the decision. That consistency is what makes practice results transferable.

title: 15 · Auto-pilot IV — don't chase & keep score
steps: The don't-chase gates

Three optional filters that stop the scanner buying excitement: 🟢 green day only, skip RSI ≥ 70, and skip day-jump > X%. All three answer the same question — is this a setup, or a party we're arriving at late? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' buy must clear EVERY gate you switch on - excitement is filtered out</text></svg>
🟢 Green day only
Only buy shares that closed UP today. A red close means the day's sellers won; buying tomorrow's open against that is catching a knife. A cheap filter with a big behaviour change.
Skip RSI ≥ 70

RSI at 70+ means the share has already run hard for two weeks — the 'overbought' zone. Great shares get there, but NEW entries there have poor odds: you're buying closer to the pause than to the start. This gate waits for the cool-down.
Skip day-jump > X%

Your buy fills at TOMORROW'S open — so a share already up, say, 12% TODAY means paying top price for a spent move. Set 5 and any candidate up more than 5% today is passed over. 5–8% is a sensible range: loose enough to catch momentum building, tight enough to skip the vertical ones. Blank = off. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='52' width='15' height='12' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='54' y='54' width='15' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='88' y='50' width='15' height='14' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='122' y='53' width='15' height='11' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='156' y='18' width='15' height='46' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><text x='163' y='12' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>today: +12% - the move is SPENT</text><line x1='196' y1='18' x2='250' y2='18' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='0'/><circle cx='236' cy='30' r='3.5' fill='#f87171'/><text x='246' y='34' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>your fill: tomorrow’s</text><text x='246' y='44' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>OPEN - top price</text><text x='20' y='86' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>skip day-jump > 5%: the robot refuses to chase what already ran</text></svg>
Gates stack — and only guard the scanner
A candidate must clear EVERY gate you've switched on. 🎯 My Picks ignore the gates entirely: a pick is your own limit price, so chasing is impossible by construction.
🤖 The Bot Scoreboard

The Scoreboard grades ONLY the robot's own closed trades — your manual trades are kept separate. It shows trades, win rate, average win % vs average loss %, profit factor, and expectancy: the average % result per trade. It is your rule-set's report card.
Expectancy, in one breath

Expectancy = (win rate × average win) − (loss rate × average loss). Positive = your rules make money on average per trade. Negative = they lose slowly, no matter how good any single week feels. It's THE number — everything else is commentary. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 92' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='160' y='16' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>expectancy - one honest number per trade</text><rect x='14' y='26' width='130' height='28' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='79' y='38' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>win rate × avg win</text><text x='79' y='49' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>what winning gives</text><text x='160' y='44' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='15' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>−</text><rect x='176' y='26' width='130' height='28' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='241' y='38' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>loss rate × avg loss</text><text x='241' y='49' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>what losing takes</text><text x='160' y='72' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>positive = your rules make money on average - the graduation test</text><text x='160' y='84' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>20+ closed robot trades, fees included, before it means anything</text></svg>
The graduation test

Let the bot run for 20+ closed trades. Positive expectancy including fees? Your rules have earned the next conversation. Negative? Congratulations — the simulator just saved you real money. Tune ONE rule at a time and run the next batch. Most first rule-sets fail; that's the system working.
Pre-set combos and the 🎣 dip entry

The scanner can demand a COMBO before buying: curated pairs (🚀 Breakout + 🏦 Big money?, 🚀 + 🔷 Block day…), the accumulation→ignition sequences (🏦 or 🕵️ in the prior 3 days, then 🚀 today), or — the mathematically honest choice — 📋 ADAPTIVE: only buy when the candidate is firing a pair that is currently SOLID on YOUR report card, re-checked every data day. A 'best combo' frozen from one good week goes stale; the card-driven gate can't. And instead of buying the next open, 🎣 patient entry places a limit X% under the last close — use the 📉 Dip Finder first: it measures the share's REAL median dip, how often each depth fills, and what happened +5 days AFTER fills (deeper fills less often, and fills cluster on weak days — see the trade-off before you choose).

quiz.q: Why does buying a share that's already up 12% TODAY usually go badly in this app?
a: The app charges extra for it
Your fill is TOMORROW'S OPEN — you'd pay top price for a move that already happened, right as early buyers sell to you
quiz.why: End-of-day signal, next-open fill. The later you arrive in a move, the more you're the exit liquidity. The day-jump gate automates walking away.

quiz.q: Gates on: 🟢 green only, RSI skip, day-jump 5. A candidate closed up +3%, RSI 62, green day. Does the scanner consider it?
a: Yes — it clears all three: green ✓, RSI 62 < 70 ✓, +3% under the 5% limit ✓
quiz.why: Gates are pass/fail per candidate. Clear them all and normal scoring takes over.

quiz.q: Scoreboard: 12 trades, win rate 42%, avg win +9%, avg loss −4%. What's the expectancy telling you?
a: Negative — a win rate under 50% means losing
(0.42 × 9) − (0.58 × 4) ≈ +1.5% per trade — POSITIVE. Modest win rate, but wins are twice the size of losses
quiz.why: 3.78 − 2.32 = +1.46% per trade. Profitable strategies with sub-50% win rates are everywhere — the SIZE of wins versus losses decides.

quiz.q: After 25 bot trades your expectancy is −0.8%. The smart next move?
a: Go to real money anyway — it'll be different
Be glad you found out for free; change ONE rule (add a gate, widen the trail…) and run the next batch — one change at a time
quiz.why: Negative expectancy discovered in practice is the system succeeding. Change one variable per batch, or you'll never know which change mattered.

title: 16 · Reports & AI review
steps: The share report

Tap 🖨 Report on any row, a code in Top 20, or a share in any report list, for a one-page report: price, a plain-English summary, signals, recent history, and official links. At the top of every report you'll find two buttons side by side: 🖨 Print / Save as PDF and 🔬 Research further — both visible straight away. The report opens inside the app on every device — one window, nothing separate juggling on top. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 108' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='20' y='8' width='120' height='92' rx='6' fill='rgba(58,74,122,.12)' stroke='#3a4a7a' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='80' y='22' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>SHARE REPORT</text><line x1='30' y1='28' x2='130' y2='28' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1'/><text x='34' y='40' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>price + day move</text><text x='34' y='52' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>plain-English summary</text><text x='34' y='64' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>every signal + rating</text><text x='34' y='76' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>range + volume picture</text><text x='34' y='90' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>your note</text><text x='160' y='34' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='9' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>one page,</text><text x='160' y='48' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='9' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>everything known</text><text x='160' y='66' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>print / save as PDF</text><text x='160' y='80' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>notes appear on</text><text x='160' y='92' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>the printout</text></svg>
The price chart

Tap 📊 on any row (or in the Deep dive) for the chart. Switch 🕯 Candles/📈 Line, pick 1M–1Y–Max, and touch or hover any day for its open/high/low/close and volume. Gold dots mark accumulation days, a dashed line shows normal volume so surges pop, 'vs mkt' overlays an index ETF, and Log scale tames big movers. Best part: if you've paper-traded the share, your ▲ buys, ▼ sells, 🎯 target and 🛑 stop are drawn right on the price — review your decisions where they happened.
Print or save as PDF

Every report and list has a 🖨 Print / PDF button. It opens inside the app with its own 'Print / Save as PDF' button — tap that and just the report prints (or saves as PDF), not the screen behind it. This works for the share report, Top 20, portfolio and watchlist.
Add your notes
Every report has a 📝 My notes box — type why you're watching a share before printing, and it appears on the printout. Leave it blank for ruled lines to write on by hand.
Free AI deep-dive

The report has a 📋 Copy AI prompt button. Tap it, paste into Claude or ChatGPT, and get a balanced AI review — for free, using an AI you already have open. The prompt asks for both the bullish and bearish case and no buy/sell advice. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 88' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='26' width='88' height='34' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='54' y='42' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Copy AI</text><text x='54' y='53' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>prompt</text><line x1='98' y1='43' x2='130' y2='43' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='124,39 132,43 124,47' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='134' y='26' width='88' height='34' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='178' y='42' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>paste into</text><text x='178' y='53' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Claude / ChatGPT</text><line x1='222' y1='43' x2='254' y2='43' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='248,39 256,43 248,47' fill='#8fa0c9'/><text x='285' y='40' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>balanced</text><text x='285' y='52' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>second look</text><text x='160' y='78' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>free - it uses an account you already have; still not advice</text></svg>
Offline & speed
Once you've pressed ⬇ Download all, a 📂 Load from saved data button appears — instant loading with no network. Great for slow-network days.
Room to read: ⛶ Max and 🖥 Full screen

Every report window has two size buttons in its footer. ⛶ Max grows the window to fill the app. 🖥 Full screen goes further — the report takes over your entire monitor (great for charts and long tables). Esc, tapping 🖥 again, or closing the window brings everything back exactly as it was.

quiz.q: The printer icon on a share opens…
a: A one-page printable research sheet with the key stats and official links
quiz.why: Print it, write your notes on it, and verify with the official links before deciding anything.

quiz.q: The 📋 Copy AI prompt asks an AI for…
a: A balanced bullish AND bearish case, with no advice
quiz.why: Both sides of the story, from an AI you already use — informing you, never deciding for you.

quiz.q: A report feels cramped on a laptop screen. Fastest fix?
a: Tap 🖥 Full screen in the report's footer — Esc brings you back
quiz.why: 🖥 Full screen hands the report the whole monitor and one key (Esc) returns you. ⛶ Max is the halfway option inside the app window.

title: 17 · Reading signals together
steps: No single number decides anything

Each rating answers a different question. One on its own is weak; several agreeing is what's interesting. The skill is reading them TOGETHER — and then verifying with real announcements before you conclude anything.
A 'quiet accumulation' picture

The classic pattern worth researching: a high Accumulation count, a Watch Score of 7+, a modest daily move — NOT a huge spike — and no obvious news yet. That combination suggests steady buying that hasn't been noticed. It can still be index buying, so it's a lead, not proof. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='160' y='14' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the ‘quiet accumulation’ picture - three gauges agreeing</text><rect x='14' y='24' width='90' height='44' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='59' y='40' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Accum 7/10</text><text x='59' y='56' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>steady buying</text><rect x='115' y='24' width='90' height='44' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='160' y='40' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Score 7+</text><text x='160' y='56' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>strong overall</text><rect x='216' y='24' width='90' height='44' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='261' y='40' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>small daily</text><text x='261' y='56' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>moves - calm</text><text x='160' y='86' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>several agreeing = worth researching; one alone = weak</text></svg>
A 'something just happened' picture

A big Sharp Mover score (large move × heavy volume) plus a 📢 likely-news flag usually means an announcement dropped. Here your FIRST click is the 🏛 announcements link to find out what — the numbers only tell you it moved, never whether the news is good or bad.
A 'be careful' picture

Price near the top of its range (position 85%+), a long up-streak, and volume now fading is an extended move — the easy gains may already be gone. High numbers are not automatically good; context decides. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='10,74 50,66 90,58 130,46 170,38 210,30 250,26 300,24' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><rect x='238' y='12' width='70' height='20' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='273' y='26' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>range top 85%+</text><rect x='180' y='74' width='13' height='22' rx='1.5' fill='#f5c84c'/><rect x='210' y='78' width='13' height='18' rx='1.5' fill='#f5c84c'/><rect x='240' y='84' width='13' height='12' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='270' y='88' width='13' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><text x='160' y='96' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='1' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'></text><text x='14' y='20' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>long streak up…</text><text x='96' y='90' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>…but volume now FADING</text><text x='232' y='44' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>extended: the easy</text><text x='232' y='54' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>gains may be behind it</text></svg>
Direction matters on volume

Heavy volume with price UP = buyers in control. The same heavy volume with price DOWN = heavy SELLING, which is the opposite story. Always check the colour/direction, not just the size of the volume surge. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='40' y='20' width='18' height='34' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><polyline points='24,36 46,26 68,32 90,20' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2'/><text x='66' y='74' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>heavy volume, price UP</text><text x='66' y='86' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>= buyers in control</text><rect x='232' y='20' width='18' height='34' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><polyline points='216,20 238,30 260,26 282,38' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='2'/><text x='258' y='74' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>SAME volume, price DOWN</text><text x='258' y='86' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>= heavy selling</text><line x1='160' y1='16' x2='160' y2='62' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='3 3'/></svg>
Always end at the source

Every reading above is an estimate from price and volume. The last step is never 'the app said so' — it's opening the announcements or news link and reading what actually happened. Treat the app as the thing that tells you WHERE to look, not what to do.

quiz.q: The strongest research lead is…
a: A hot tip from a forum
quiz.why: One signal is weak; agreement between different measures is what's interesting — and it still needs verifying.

quiz.q: Heavy volume while the price FALLS means…
a: Heavy selling — the opposite story to heavy buying
quiz.why: Always check direction before size. The same crowd that pushes prices up can be rushing for the exit.

quiz.q: Three moderate signals fire together on one share: a multi-day price streak, volume well above average, and a high accumulation count. How should you read that?
a: Ignore — each signal is only moderate
Several independent patterns pointing the same way is stronger evidence than one loud signal — worth a research look
Buy immediately — three signals is confirmation
quiz.why: Independent evidence agreeing is how conviction should build — but it still earns research, not an automatic buy.

steps: 1 · Load

Tap ⚡ Get today's fresh prices. When fresh data lands, 🔔 What’s changed for me opens once by itself IF anything matters in YOUR lists — targets or stops near, big moves, confirmed news. 2 · Scan

Run the scans that match how you think: 🎯 Best Evidence Today for shares carrying graded, proven signals, 🔥 Volume Surge for unusual activity, 🏆 Top 20 to Watch for the evidence-first shortlist. Tap a share code to open its report.
3 · Shortlist & note
Star the ones worth watching (⭐) so they land in your watchlist. Open a report on any that stand out, type a note on WHY you're watching it, and save or print it.
4 · Verify, then decide for yourself

For anything interesting, open the 🏛 announcements and 📰 news links and read the real story. Optionally tap 📋 Copy AI prompt for a balanced second opinion. The app and the AI both inform you — the decision, and the responsibility, stay with you.
Let the briefing come to you

Once per fresh data day, 🔔 What's changed for me opens by itself when there's something worth saying about YOUR holdings, orders and watchlist — targets near or hit, stops threatened, big moves, confirmed news, and what 🤖 Auto-pilot did overnight. Tap any line to deep-dive. If it doesn't open, there was nothing important — that's a feature, not a fault. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 84' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='14' y='20' width='120' height='44' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='74' y='38' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>🔔 What’s changed</text><text x='74' y='54' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>for me</text><line x1='134' y1='42' x2='166' y2='42' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='160,38 168,42 160,46' fill='#8fa0c9'/><text x='240' y='32' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>opens by itself once per</text><text x='240' y='44' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>fresh data day - only about</text><text x='240' y='56' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>YOUR shares and watchlist</text><text x='160' y='78' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>exits near · big moves · confirmed news - read this first</text></svg>

quiz.q: The sensible daily order is…
a: Load → scan → shortlist → verify with the announcements
quiz.why: The app makes the first three steps one tap each — the verify step is yours, and it's the one that matters.

quiz.q: Once your data is saved, the daily routine takes…
a: A few minutes — loading is instant and scans are one tap
quiz.why: Saved data loads in seconds; fresh prices arrive in the background while you read.

quiz.q: Why does the 🔔 briefing sometimes NOT appear?
a: Nothing about YOUR shares changed enough to be worth interrupting you — silence is information too
quiz.why: The briefing opens only when it has something to say about your positions or watchlist. No noise for noise's sake.

title: 19 · Filtering & finding shares
steps: Why filter

The whole exchange is thousands of shares. Filters cut it down to just the ones that match what you care about — a price range you can afford, a minimum volume, or only ordinary shares (no ETFs/options). It turns a wall of data into a short, workable list. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 104' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path d='M 40 14 L 280 14 L 200 52 L 200 84 L 120 84 L 120 52 Z' fill='rgba(58,74,122,.15)' stroke='#3a4a7a' stroke-width='1.3'/><text x='160' y='28' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='9' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>thousands of shares</text><text x='160' y='48' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>price · volume · type · liquidity · RSI</text><text x='160' y='72' fill='#4ade80' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>your handful</text><text x='160' y='98' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>filters cut the exchange down to only what you care about</text></svg>
Open the filters

Look for 'Refine filters' or 'Show advanced filters'. Inside are a price range, volume thresholds, and share-type checkboxes. Hover any field (in training mode) to see exactly what it does, then press Apply.
Liquidity & RSI — the pro filters

Two filters worth knowing. In the Type tab, Liquidity — $ traded/day (average daily volume × price) screens out thinly-traded shares that are hard to buy or sell at a fair price; set a floor like ≥$250k a day and it quietly applies to every view. In the Signals tab, RSI zone shows only Oversold (≤30 — beaten down, maybe due a bounce), Neutral, or Overbought (≥70 — run hard, maybe due a pause). Mix either with the other filters to narrow the list. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='30' y='52' width='20' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><text x='40' y='76' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>$8k/day</text><text x='40' y='88' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>hard to get OUT of</text><rect x='130' y='26' width='20' height='34' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><text x='140' y='76' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>$900k/day</text><text x='140' y='88' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>easy in, easy out</text><line x1='210' y1='16' x2='210' y2='88' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='3 3'/><text x='264' y='36' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Liquidity filter:</text><text x='264' y='50' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>avg volume × price</text><text x='264' y='64' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>skips shares too thin</text><text x='264' y='76' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>to realistically trade</text></svg>
Search by name or code
The search box filters instantly as you type — type a code (BHP) or part of a company name. It works on the main list and inside your watchlist.
Sort to surface the best
Tap a column header, or use the sort dropdown, to order by Watch Score, Volume Surge, % change, and so on. Sorting by Vol Surge quickly floats the day's unusual movers to the top.
Save it as My Report
Once you've dialled in filters you like, press 💾 Save to store them as ⭐ My Report — then ⚡ Auto-run so the app lands on that exact view every time it loads. No re-setting filters each day.

quiz.q: Filters exist to…
a: Cut thousands of shares down to a short list matching what you care about
quiz.why: A wall of data becomes a workable list: your price range, your volume floor, your share types.

quiz.q: 💾 Save under ⭐ My Report keeps…
a: Your exact filter setup, for one tap next time — with Auto-run it applies on every load
quiz.why: Dial it in once, land on your view every day.

quiz.q: You want to skip shares that barely trade. Which filter does that honestly?
quiz.why: $ traded/day = volume × price — how much money actually changes hands. A floor like ≥$250k skips shares you couldn't buy or sell at a fair price.

title: 20 · Keeping your data safe
steps: Where your data lives

Your watchlist, portfolio and settings are saved on THIS device, in this browser — not in the cloud. That keeps it private and free, but it means the browser can clear it, especially on phones (iPhone/Safari is the worst for wiping storage overnight). <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='30' y='12' width='70' height='74' rx='10' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><rect x='44' y='20' width='42' height='50' rx='3' fill='rgba(58,74,122,.2)' stroke='#3a4a7a' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='65' y='38' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>watchlist</text><text x='65' y='50' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>portfolio</text><text x='65' y='62' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>settings</text><circle cx='65' cy='79' r='3' fill='#54627f'/><text x='210' y='30' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>everything lives on THIS device,</text><text x='210' y='44' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>in THIS browser - private, free,</text><text x='210' y='58' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>works offline</text><text x='210' y='78' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>(so protect the device copy - next steps)</text></svg>
The big fix: install to home screen

Add the app to your home screen (Android/Chrome: ⋮ → Add to Home screen · iPhone/Safari: Share → Add to Home Screen). An installed app gets durable storage the browser won't casually clear — this is the single best thing you can do to stop losing your lists.
It backs itself up

The app keeps an automatic on-device backup of your watchlist and portfolio and restores them if they go missing. There are also manual buttons: ↩ Restore from backup (⚙ Lists) and a gold Restore my portfolio button in the Portfolio.
Download for offline

Press ⬇ Download / update once to save the whole exchange's history to your device — the first time is the slow part. After that it's a smart update: pressing it again only fetches the new days and adds them, so it's fast. Your normal daily load also tops up today's data automatically, so your saved history stays current and keeps growing deeper (better signals over time).
Share saved data between devices

In ⚙ Setup & data, ⬆ Export saved data to file saves all your downloaded markets. For a small amount you can Copy and paste it; for a big download it saves a file to your device — move it across by email, cloud, or cable. On the other device use ⬇ Import saved data from file (or “Or paste copied data”). No account or server needed; each exchange stays separate.

quiz.q: Your watchlist and portfolio live…
a: In the cloud on a server
On THIS device, in this browser — private and free
quiz.why: Nothing leaves your device. The trade-off: browsers can clear storage, so read the next question.

quiz.q: The single best protection against a phone wiping your lists?
a: Install the app to your home screen — installed apps get durable storage
quiz.why: Add to Home Screen is one tap and makes your storage far harder for the browser to casually clear.

quiz.q: Where does your portfolio and watchlist data live?
a: On this device, in your browser's storage — export a backup file for safekeeping
quiz.why: Everything stays on YOUR device. That's private — but it means a backup export is your responsibility (the app also keeps an automatic local backup with a gold ↩ restore button).

title: 21 · The Research Further list
steps: What it's for

While going through reports and scans you'll hit shares that look interesting but you're not ready to commit to. The 🔬 Research Further list is a holding pen for those — a to-do list of shares to look into later, kept separate from your watchlist so it doesn't clutter it.
How it's different from a watchlist

Your watchlist is a collection you keep and track. The research list is a worklist you clear: flag → research → decide. Think of it as sticky notes saying “look into this”, not shares you're actively following.
Flagging a share

Open any share's report — the 🔬 Research further button sits right at the top, next to Print, so it's visible straight away. Tap it and it asks (optionally) why it caught your eye — a quick note like “volume spike” or “near 52wk low”. That note is what stops the list becoming a mystery in a week's time.
Working through the list

Open the 🔬 Research button (in Advanced, in the Instant Reports row) to see everything you've parked, newest first, with how long ago you flagged each. Stale ones (over a week) show their date in red as a gentle nudge.
Deciding: promote or clear

For each share: 📄 Open report to dig in, ★ To watchlist to promote the keepers (moves it across and clears it here), or ✓ Done to remove ones that didn't pan out. The point is to keep it moving — it's a to-do list, not a second watchlist.

quiz.q: The 🔬 Research list is…
a: A to-do pen: flag it → research it → promote it or clear it
quiz.why: Sticky notes saying 'look into this' — the point is to keep it moving, not to collect.

quiz.q: When you finish researching a parked share you…
a: ★ promote the keepers to the watchlist, ✓ clear the rest
quiz.why: Promote or clear — a research list that only grows is a guilt list.

quiz.q: What's the point of the note the 🔬 Research further flag asks for?
a: It records why the share caught your eye, so next week the list isn't a mystery
quiz.why: 'Volume spike', 'near 52wk low' — the note is future-you's memory. Reviewing WHY beats staring at a bare list of codes.

title: 22 · Bullish & Bearish, and quick filters
steps: The stats bar
Along the top of your results is a row of counts: Showing, Gainers, Losers, Vol ≥200%, Quiet buying?, Up 2+ Days, and — added recently — Bullish and Bearish. Each is tappable to filter.
What Bullish / Bearish mean

Bullish counts shares showing buying-side patterns: accumulating, buying pressure, an up-streak, or up hard on heavy volume. Bearish counts selling-side patterns: falling on heavy volume, distribution, or sinking near their lows. It's a data summary of what price and volume did — not a prediction or advice.
Tap to filter your current view

Tapping any stat narrows whatever you're already looking at — a scan result, a report, your list — instead of resetting to the whole market. This works inside the Starter-view pop-up reports too: run a scan, then tap Bullish to see just the bullish ones within it.
Combine and clear

Toggles combine — tap Gainers then Vol ≥200% to see gainers on heavy volume. Tap a lit stat again to switch it off, or tap Showing to clear them all and get your full view back. Running a new scan starts fresh.

quiz.q: Tapping BULLISH in the stats bar…
a: Filters your CURRENT view down to buying-pattern shares
quiz.why: The stat chips narrow whatever you're already looking at — even inside a scan's results.

quiz.q: The Bullish and Bearish counts are…
a: Data summaries of what price and volume actually did
quiz.why: They describe the day that already happened. What happens next is exactly what they can't know.

quiz.q: A share shows heavy volume with the price DOWN hard — a red Vol Surge chip. What is that?
a: Heavy SELLING — big volume on a falling price is money leaving, not accumulating
quiz.why: Volume shows conviction in whichever direction the price moved. Red chip = heavy selling pressure. A big-volume fall is never a bullish accumulation signal.

title: 23 · First-run setup made easy
steps: The welcome wizard

The very first time the app opens, a short wizard welcomes you and lets you pick your market, then loads it — no keys or setup to worry about. It only ever appears once. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='8' y='30' width='74' height='34' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='45' y='46' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>welcome</text><text x='45' y='57' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>wizard</text><line x1='82' y1='47' x2='102' y2='47' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='96,43 104,47 96,51' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='106' y='30' width='74' height='34' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='143' y='46' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>pick your</text><text x='143' y='57' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>market</text><line x1='180' y1='47' x2='200' y2='47' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='194,43 202,47 194,51' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='204' y='30' width='74' height='34' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='241' y='46' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>loaded -</text><text x='241' y='57' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>ready to go</text><path d='M 143 64 L 143 82 L 290 82' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><text x='216' y='78' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>or ‘show me a demo first’ - sample shares, no setup</text><text x='160' y='16' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>first open: no keys, no signup - two taps and the market is in</text></svg>
Prefer to look around first?
On the welcome step you can tap “Just show me a demo first” to explore with sample shares before you load the real market. Nothing is blocked while you look around.
Tidier settings afterwards

Once you're set up, ⚙ Setup & data keeps the everyday things visible (exchange, load, download, export) and folds the technical bits — news key, volume window, startup automation, presets — into a collapsed ⚙ Advanced settings section. Tap to expand any of it when you need to.

quiz.q: Want to look around before loading the real market?
a: 'Just show me a demo first' lets you explore with sample shares
quiz.why: Nothing is blocked while you look around — tap 'demo' any time, then ⚡ Load when you want the live market.

quiz.q: The welcome wizard appears…
a: Only the very first time the app opens
quiz.why: Three quick steps, once. After that the app remembers everything.

quiz.q: The ⬇ 'Download all data' button is dimmed and says 'load an exchange first'. What's happening?
a: It needs an exchange loaded before it can bulk-download — the button names the missing step and undims when ready
quiz.why: The bulk download just needs an exchange loaded first — the button literally tells you when it's ready.

title: 24 · Common mistakes to avoid
steps: Treating a score as a 'buy'

A high Watch Score or a big Sharp Mover number means 'unusual — worth a look', never 'good buy'. The app measures what price and volume did; it can't know if it's good news or bad. Always your call, after research. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 88' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='14' y='18' width='90' height='44' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='59' y='36' fill='#4ade80' font-size='10' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Score 9.5</text><text x='59' y='52' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>very unusual</text><line x1='104' y1='40' x2='136' y2='40' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='130,36 138,40 130,44' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='140' y='18' width='80' height='44' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='180' y='36' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>‘worth</text><text x='180' y='50' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a look’</text><text x='262' y='30' fill='#f87171' font-size='10' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>NOT</text><text x='262' y='44' fill='#f87171' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>‘good buy’</text><text x='160' y='80' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the app measures unusual - it cannot know if unusual is good</text></svg>
Ignoring volume direction
A huge Volume Surge with the price DOWN is heavy SELLING, not a bargain. Check the colour (🟢 up / 🔴 down) before you get excited about a big volume number.
Chasing an extended move
A share near the top of its range (position 85%+) after a long up-streak may have already made its move. High-and-late is a common trap — the easy gains can be gone.
Skipping the announcement

The app's 'news' flag is an estimate from price/volume unless it carries a ✓ (then it's a confirmed ASX announcement). Either way, never conclude 'it moved on news' without opening the announcements link and reading what actually happened.
Forgetting it's end-of-day
Every figure is from the last close and may be delayed — it is not live intraday data. Don't treat it as a real-time trading screen.
Chasing — buying AFTER the move

The classic beginner loss: a share jumps 15%, it's all over the news, you buy the excitement — and you've paid top price for a move that already happened. Big up-days are often followed by a pull-back as early buyers take profit. The don't-chase toolkit in 🤖 Auto-pilot (green-day-only, skip RSI ≥ 70, skip day-jump) exists because this mistake is so common — copy those rules even when buying manually. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='10,74 50,72 90,68 130,62 170,26 210,34 250,44 300,52' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><text x='120' y='18' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>+15% day - all over the news</text><circle cx='192' cy='30' r='4' fill='#f87171'/><text x='214' y='22' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>you buy HERE</text><text x='230' y='64' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>…and ride it back down</text><text x='160' y='94' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the move already happened - excitement is the most expensive signal</text></svg>
Betting the farm on one share

Putting half your account in one 'sure thing' means one piece of bad news can undo months of good decisions. The 📦 max-per-share rule exists for exactly this. Professionals think survival first: no single position should be able to really hurt you. 5–15% per share is a common practice range. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='62' cy='46' r='30' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='9'/><path d='M 62 16 A 30 30 0 1 1 33 55' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='9'/><text x='62' y='84' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>half in one ‘sure thing’</text><circle cx='222' cy='46' r='30' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='9'/><path d='M 222 16 A 30 30 0 0 1 248 30' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='9'/><path d='M 250 34 A 30 30 0 0 1 250 58' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='9'/><path d='M 248 62 A 30 30 0 0 1 222 76' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='9'/><text x='222' y='90' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>spread - one bad day cannot sink you</text><text x='150' y='14' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>one news release vs months of good decisions</text></svg>

quiz.q: A huge Volume Surge with the price DOWN is…
a: Heavy selling — check the direction before getting excited
quiz.why: The most common beginner trap in this app: big volume number, wrong direction.

quiz.q: A news flag WITHOUT a ✓ is…
a: An estimate from price and volume — open the announcements link before concluding anything
quiz.why: The ✓ is the tell: with it you're reading facts from the ASX feed; without it, an educated guess.

quiz.q: A share is up 14% today on hot news and you feel the urge to jump in. What's the experienced move?
a: Buy fast before it goes higher
Recognise the FOMO: the move has happened and late buyers fund early sellers' exits. Watchlist it and wait for a settle or pullback
quiz.why: Chasing extended moves is the most reliable way to buy tops. If it's a real trend there'll be calmer entries; if it isn't, you've dodged the fade.

title: 25 · Reading the price chart
steps: Open it anywhere

Tap 📊 on any share row, or from the Deep dive, to open the price chart. Pick a window — 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y or Max — and touch (or hover) any day to see its exact date, open/high/low/close, volume and % move. Works with your finger on phones.
Line or candles

📈 Line shows closing prices — clean and calm. 🕯 Candles show each day's full story: the body runs from open to close (green = closed up, red = closed down) and the thin wicks mark the day's high and low. Long wicks mean a battle happened; gaps between candles mean the price jumped overnight.
