The app remembers which view you prefer. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 104' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='56' y='28' width='10' height='40' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><line x1='61' y1='16' x2='61' y2='28' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.6'/><line x1='61' y1='68' x2='61' y2='80' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.6'/><text x='84' y='24' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>high (wick)</text><text x='84' y='36' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>close (top - green day)</text><text x='84' y='62' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>open (bottom)</text><text x='84' y='80' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>low (wick)</text><rect x='216' y='32' width='10' height='36' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><line x1='221' y1='20' x2='221' y2='32' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.6'/><line x1='221' y1='68' x2='221' y2='78' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.6'/><text x='244' y='36' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>red day:</text><text x='244' y='48' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>open on top,</text><text x='244' y='60' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>close below</text><text x='160' y='98' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>one candle = one day’s full story; a line shows only the closes</text></svg>
The overlays

MA20 (blue) and MA50 (purple) are 20- and 50-day average prices — price above a rising average is trending up. The shaded box is the current 4-week trading range over the recent weeks. Gold dots underneath mark ACCUMULATION days — up days on 50%+ above-normal volume — so you can see the app's core signal on the price itself. In the volume strip, the dashed line is normal volume: bars towering over it are the surges.
vs market & log scale

Tap vs mkt to overlay an index ETF (VAS, A200, STW or IOZ) indexed to the same start — if the share only matched the dashed line, it rode the market rather than beating it. Tap Log for shares that have multiplied: equal % moves get equal height, so the early move isn't squashed flat.
Your trades, on the chart

If you've paper-traded the share, your ▲ buys and ▼ sells are drawn at the exact date and price, with dashed 🎯 target and 🛑 stop lines while you hold it. Reviewing a closed trade where it happened — did you buy the top? sell the bottom? — teaches more than any statistic.
A chart is history, not prophecy

Everything on the chart already happened. Patterns suggest, they never promise — a support level can hold or break, and end-of-day data can't tell you which. Use the chart to understand what HAS happened, the announcements to understand why, and keep every decision your own.

quiz.q: The gold dots under the price chart mark…
a: Accumulation days — up days on 50%+ above-normal volume
quiz.why: The app's core signal, drawn on the price itself so you can see where the quiet buying happened.

quiz.q: A chart can show you…
a: Only what has already happened — patterns suggest, they never promise
quiz.why: A support level can hold or break, and end-of-day data can't tell you which. History informs; it doesn't guarantee.

quiz.q: When is the log scale worth switching on?
a: For shares that have multiplied several times — equal % moves get equal height, so the early move isn't squashed flat
quiz.why: On a normal scale a 10× share's early doubling looks flat. Log scale gives every equal % move equal height — the honest way to read big movers.

title: 26 · The Signals column & confirmed filings
steps: What the Signals column is

The right-hand SIGNALS column holds the app's pattern flags. Most shares show '— none' most days — that's normal and healthy. A flag only appears when a scan detects something unusual, which is exactly what makes the flags worth reading when they do show up. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 88' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='20' width='38' height='20' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='29' y='33' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>- none</text><rect x='54' y='20' width='38' height='20' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='73' y='33' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>- none</text><rect x='98' y='20' width='38' height='20' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='117' y='33' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>- none</text><rect x='142' y='20' width='38' height='20' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='161' y='33' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>- none</text><rect x='186' y='20' width='38' height='20' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='205' y='33' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>- none</text><rect x='230' y='20' width='38' height='20' rx='4' fill='rgba(245,200,76,.18)' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='249' y='33' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>flag!</text><text x='160' y='62' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>‘- none’ most days is NORMAL and healthy</text><text x='160' y='76' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a flag is rare by design - that is exactly what makes it worth reading</text></svg>
The estimate flags

🕵️ Informed? = steady buying footprint (rising on heavy volume). 🏦 Big money? = the same at institutional size (traders: institutional accumulation). 🔷 Blk = a block-trade-sized volume day, with ▲/▼ showing direction. 🚀 Breakout = closed above its stored-year high on above-average volume. 📉 Quiet selling? (traders: distribution) = the bearish mirror — falling on heavy volume. 🥇 Vol record = today is the highest volume in its stored history. ⤴ MA cross = the 20-day average price crossed above the 50-day today. Every one of these is an ESTIMATE from price and volume — a reason to look, never a verdict.
Confirmed filings — the ✓ tags

When the official ASX announcements feed is reachable, the app upgrades estimates to facts for the shares on screen: 🧑‍💼 Director ✓ means a real director-interest filing (Appendix 3Y) hit the ASX in the last 5 days — open it to see whether it was a buy or a sell. In the News column, 📢 News ✓ and 🔇 Quiet ✓ mean the answer came from the real announcements list, with the latest headline shown when you hover. No ✓ means you're looking at the estimate — the app always tells you which is which. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='20' width='130' height='48' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='75' y='36' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>ESTIMATE flags</text><text x='75' y='50' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a footprint in price</text><text x='75' y='61' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>and volume - a guess</text><line x1='140' y1='44' x2='172' y2='44' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='166,40 174,44 166,48' fill='#4ade80'/><rect x='176' y='20' width='134' height='48' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='243' y='36' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✓ CONFIRMED tags</text><text x='243' y='50' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>an actual filing exists</text><text x='243' y='61' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>(what it MEANS: still read it)</text><text x='160' y='86' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>when the announcements feed is reachable, estimates upgrade to facts</text></svg>
The golden rule, again

Confirmed tells you a filing exists; it never tells you what it means. An Appendix 3Y can be a sale. A price-sensitive announcement can be bad news. Tap 📄 Verify, read the actual document, and make up your own mind — the flags only point the torch.
Who's actually buying — the ownership callout

Deep Dive includes a 'Who's actually buying?' section: the share's estimated footprint flags (🕵️ informed-style, 🏦 institutional-style, block trades) with honest labels, plus one-tap searches for the REAL facts — director trades, substantial-holder notices and top-20 shareholder lists. Footprints are estimates from price/volume; filings are facts. The callout keeps the two clearly apart.

quiz.q: 🧑‍💼 Director ✓ means…
a: An estimate that a director might be buying
A CONFIRMED director-interest filing on the ASX — which could be a buy OR a sell
quiz.why: Confirmed tells you a filing exists, never what it means — open it and read whether they bought or sold.

quiz.q: Most shares show '— none' in Signals because…
a: Flags only appear when a scan detects something unusual — rare is the point
quiz.why: If every share flagged every day, the flags would mean nothing. Silence is the healthy default.

quiz.q: Deep Dive shows '🏦 Big money?' on a share. Where do you check whether institutions REALLY hold it?
a: Tap the ownership links — substantial-holder notices and the top-20 shareholder list are the facts; the flag is only the footprint
quiz.why: Sub-5% holdings aren't even publicly disclosed on the ASX, so the flag can only ever be an estimate. Filings and the top-20 register are the checkable truth.

title: 27 · The report card — the app marks its own homework
steps: Why an app would grade itself

Every scanner on earth shows you its hits. This app also shows you its misses. The 📋 Signal report card re-runs every flag formula over your own saved history and asks one blunt question: after a flag fired, did those shares actually do better than the market? Some weeks the honest answer is no — and it says so, in red. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='14' width='146' height='68' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='83' y='30' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>every other scanner</text><text x='83' y='48' fill='#4ade80' font-size='11' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓</text><text x='83' y='66' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>shows you its hits</text><rect x='164' y='14' width='146' height='68' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='237' y='30' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>this app’s report card</text><text x='237' y='48' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='11' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✓ ✓ ✗ ✗ ✓</text><text x='237' y='66' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>shows hits AND misses</text><text x='160' y='92' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a scanner that never confesses is an ad, not a tool</text></svg>
How the test works

It walks back through the last ~15 trading days of your saved data. Every time a flag would have fired on a share, it looks 5 trading days ahead and measures the move. All shares' moves over those same windows form the baseline — the line a flag has to beat before it can claim any credit.
Reading one line

'Fired 83 times · 5 trading days later: 25% higher · average move −3.92% (all shares: +0.13%)' translates as: it fired 83 times; only a quarter of those shares were higher a week on; on average they FELL 3.92% while the average share gained 0.13%. Verdict: did NOT beat the market. No excuses attached. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 104' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='8' y='10' width='304' height='30' rx='5' fill='rgba(58,74,122,.12)' stroke='#3a4a7a' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='16' y='29' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>fired 83×</text><text x='78' y='29' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>· 25% higher</text><text x='148' y='29' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>· avg −3.92%</text><text x='230' y='29' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>(all shares: +0.13%)</text><line x1='60' y1='40' x2='60' y2='56' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='54,52 62,56 54,60' fill='#8fa0c9'/><text x='60' y='68' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>83 experiments</text><line x1='160' y1='40' x2='160' y2='56' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='154,52 162,56 154,60' fill='#8fa0c9'/><text x='160' y='68' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>they FELL while the</text><text x='160' y='78' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>average share rose</text><line x1='268' y1='40' x2='268' y2='56' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='262,52 270,56 262,60' fill='#8fa0c9'/><text x='268' y='68' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the yardstick</text><text x='160' y='98' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>verdict: did NOT beat the market - printed with no excuses</text></svg>
The bearish flag is graded backwards

📉 Quiet selling? is a warning about selling — so for it, success means the shares it flagged went LOWER. If they rose instead, the warning failed, and the card says exactly that. One flag's red is another flag's green.
Two flags aren't graded at all

🥇 Vol record and 🔷 Block day only say 'something unusual happened here' — they don't claim a direction. The card shows their numbers but labels them direction-neutral, because grading them on direction would be pretending they promise one.
What a red fortnight really means

Flags are footprints, not prophecies. A patch where every breakout faded is real information: the market is currently punishing people who chase spikes. It doesn't mean the flags broke — and a green patch doesn't make them magic. Glance at the card every week or two and let it set how sceptical you are.
The announcement question

The card also splits every flag’s fires into 📢 news-driven (a confirmed price-sensitive announcement on the fire day or the two days before) and 🔇 quiet — and shows how many of the WINNERS had news behind them. It builds from a dated announcement log the app records as you use it, so give it a week or two of normal use; fires the log can’t vouch for are counted as unknown, never guessed.
The fine print: what the report card can't see

The card grades flags on shares still in your saved data — shares that were delisted or renamed drop out, which can flatter results slightly (the 'survivorship' effect). And a week where a flag scores badly doesn't mean the app broke — markets have regimes; momentum patterns work in some and rest in others. Use the card as a scepticism dial, not a verdict.
Combinations — when flags agree

The card's 🧩 section grades PAIRS and TRIPLES of flags that fired on the same share the same day — answering 'does 🚀 Breakout plus 🏦 Big money? actually beat either alone?'. Each combo shows its own average next to each leg's solo average, so the comparison is one glance. Combos fire less often, so samples are small: a strong combo week is a lead to keep watching across future weeks, not proof — and combos with too few fires are honestly hidden rather than shown on noise.
Two-way flags: 🥇 and 🔷 graded in both directions

🥇 Vol record and 🔷 Block day fire whether the price rose or fell — heavy volume UP is buying pressure, heavy volume DOWN is selling pressure, and averaging them together hides both stories. So the card grades each side separately: price-UP fires are judged like a bullish flag (did those shares beat the market?), price-DOWN fires are judged like a warning (did those shares fall — LOWER means the warning worked, exactly like 📉 Quiet selling?). It's the same idea as the Vol Surge chip's green vs red, applied to the report card.
Reading the new maths: edge, tiers, halves, track record

Every fire is scored against ITS OWN DAY's all-share average — the 'edge' — so a strong market week can't flatter a flag. Each line carries a confidence tier: SOLID (lots of fires, consistent edge), PROMISING (decent evidence), TOO EARLY (could still be luck). A ✓ means the edge showed up in BOTH halves of the graded window, not one lucky fortnight; 🟩/🟥 shows the edge in risk-on vs risk-off tape; and once a few weekly cards are logged, 📜 shows the line's track record ('beat in 4 of last 5 cards'). The card also grades only shares above a $50k-a-day tradeability floor — an edge that exists only on untradeable micro-caps is a phantom. Trust climbs the ladder: too early → promising → solid → persistent across cards. Capital belongs at the top rung only.

quiz.q: What question does the Signal report card actually answer?
a: After each flag fired, did those shares beat how ALL shares moved over the same days?
Which shares will go up next week?
How accurate the app's buy recommendations were
quiz.why: It re-runs every flag over your saved history and compares the aftermath against the whole market's moves over the same windows. Nothing is predicted, and the app makes no recommendations to grade — it's an honest look backwards at its own estimates.

quiz.q: For the bearish 📉 Quiet selling? flag, 'working' means the shares it flagged…
a: went LOWER — it's a warning, so falling proves the warning right
went higher, like every other flag
fired as many times as possible
quiz.why: Quiet selling? warns of heavy selling. A warning succeeds when the thing it warned about happens — so for this one flag, LOWER is the good column, and the card grades it that way round.

quiz.q: Every bullish flag shows red this fortnight. Best takeaway?
a: Be extra sceptical of flags right now — spikes are being sold into
The app is broken and the flags should be ignored forever
Nothing — results are always green if you wait
quiz.why: Results genuinely swing week to week — the card's own footer says a good or bad period proves nothing about the future. A red patch is useful market information: chasing volume pops is being punished right now. Adjust your scepticism, not your faith.

quiz.q: This week the card says Smart Money 'did NOT beat the market'. The right takeaway?
a: The app is broken — stop using it
Reverse the signals and short everything
Be extra sceptical of that flag right now; results swing with market conditions and the card exists to show you exactly that
quiz.why: The card is the app marking its own homework in YOUR saved data. Red patches mean 'lean harder on verification this week', not 'the tool failed forever'.

title: 28 · Reading the report card & the 🪜 ladder
steps: Start with the 📖 deep dive

Open 📋 Signal report card and, right at the top, tap “📖 How to read this card”. It unfolds a plain-English tour of every part — what EDGE means, the badges, the halves check, the ladder — and it remembers whether you like it open. If you only ever read one thing about the card, read that. Everything below is the hands-on version.
Hover anything to learn it

You do not have to memorise the card. Hover your mouse over any number, badge, verdict or ladder rung — or press and hold it on a phone — and a one-line explanation pops up. In training mode it is the app’s own explanation card; elsewhere it is a normal tooltip. Wander over the whole card and let it teach you in place.
The 🪜 ladder — a leaderboard of everything

At the bottom of the card is the ladder: every flag and combo lined up best-to-worst by how well it is working right now. ① Singles ranks the individual flags; ② Combinations & sequences ranks the pairs and accumulation→ignition patterns. A 🥇🥈🥉 marks the top three, a little bar shows the size, and the number on the right is the edge. Same honest maths as the rest of the card, just sorted into a quick leaderboard. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 108' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='160' y='12' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the ladder - everything ranked by how well it works NOW</text><rect x='40' y='18' width='240' height='16' rx='4' fill='rgba(74,222,128,.14)' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='50' y='29' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>1. Breakout + Vol record</text><text x='262' y='29' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>+3.6</text><rect x='40' y='38' width='240' height='16' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='50' y='49' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>2. MA cross + Block day</text><text x='262' y='49' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>+2.0</text><rect x='40' y='58' width='240' height='16' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='50' y='69' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>3. Quiet selling? (WARNING)</text><text x='262' y='69' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>+1.4</text><rect x='40' y='78' width='240' height='16' rx='4' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='50' y='89' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>9. Sharp Mover alone</text><text x='258' y='89' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>−0.9</text><text x='160' y='104' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>green on rung 3 means the WARNING works - it is not a buy</text></svg>
Green on the ladder is not always “buy”

This is the one that trips people up. Warning flags — 📉 Quiet selling? and the down-day forms of 🥇 Vol record and 🔷 Block day — score by how far price FELL. So a warning that is working ranks HIGH and shows GREEN, and it is tagged “· warning (predicts a fall)”. Green there means it is catching falls well — a reason to be careful, not a buy. Read the tag, not just the colour.
Ranked by edge in its OWN direction

That tag exists because every rung is ranked by its edge in the direction it is meant to work: a buy flag by how much its shares beat the market, a warning by how hard they fell. Mixing the two into one list only works because each is measured its own way — which is how the ladder can honestly put a bullish breakout and a bearish distribution warning on the same board.
🧩 Combinations vs ⛓ Sequences

Two different questions. 🧩 Combinations = two or three flags firing on the SAME share, the SAME day — does agreement beat any one flag alone? ⛓ Sequences = a quiet-buying flag in the 1–3 days BEFORE, then an ignition flag (🚀 breakout or ⤴ MA cross) TODAY — the classic accumulation-then-move. Both are graded exactly like singles, with the same tiers, and both need enough fires before the card will trust them.
📜 is the only rung that earns real money

A flag can top the ladder for one week on luck. The 📜 mark — “beat in 4 of last 5 cards” — is the app checking each line against the cards it saved on earlier days. A line that keeps working across weeks is the only kind of evidence that deserves real capital. Too early → promising → solid → persistent across cards: capital belongs at the top rung only, and never before 📜 agrees. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 92' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='160' y='14' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the only rung that earns real money: the track record</text><rect x='38' y='24' width='40' height='30' rx='5' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='58' y='43' fill='#4ade80' font-size='12' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✓</text><rect x='88' y='24' width='40' height='30' rx='5' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='108' y='43' fill='#4ade80' font-size='12' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✓</text><rect x='138' y='24' width='40' height='30' rx='5' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='158' y='43' fill='#f87171' font-size='12' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✗</text><rect x='188' y='24' width='40' height='30' rx='5' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='208' y='43' fill='#4ade80' font-size='12' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✓</text><rect x='238' y='24' width='40' height='30' rx='5' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='258' y='43' fill='#4ade80' font-size='12' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>✓</text><text x='160' y='70' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>beat in 4 of the last 5 saved cards</text><text x='160' y='84' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>one hot week can top the ladder on luck - weeks in a row cannot</text></svg>
🖨 Save or print a dated copy

New in this version: at the top of the card there is a 🖨 Save / print button. It opens a clean, one-page version — the deep-dive spelled out in full, every flag, every ladder rung — dated and stamped with the universe it graded. Print it, or Save as PDF, and you have a record of exactly how the signals looked today. Do it every week or two and you can watch a flag climb or fade with your own eyes, which is the whole point of a report card.
How to actually use it

A simple loop: glance at the ladder, note which one or two lines are BOTH near the top AND carry a good 📜 record, and let that set how much attention you give those flags this week. When every bullish rung is red, the market is punishing spike-chasers right now — lean harder on verification. Save a copy, and compare next fortnight. The ladder is a scepticism dial you can read at a glance, not a shopping list.

quiz.q: A warning flag like 📉 Quiet selling? is sitting near the TOP of the ladder, in green. What does that mean?
a: It is catching falls well right now — a reason for caution, not a buy
It is the best share to buy today
The ladder is broken and should be ignored
quiz.why: Warnings are ranked by how far price FELL after they fired, and tagged “· warning (predicts a fall)”. Green means the warning is working — price dropped as warned. That is a caution signal, not a green light to buy.

quiz.q: What is the difference between the 🧩 Combinations and ⛓ Sequences sections?
a: Combinations = flags on the same share the same day; Sequences = quiet buying first, then an ignition flag today
There is no difference — they are two names for the same thing
Combinations are for buying, Sequences are for selling
quiz.why: Combinations ask whether flags AGREEING on one day beats a lone flag. Sequences ask whether quiet accumulation in the days BEFORE, then an ignition flag today, is a pattern worth watching. Same maths, different question.

quiz.q: Which single thing on a ladder rung most deserves real money behind it?
a: The 📜 record — it kept working across several saved cards, not just this week
The biggest edge number, whatever its tier
A 🥇 gold medal for first place this week
quiz.why: One week tops the ladder on luck all the time. 📜 (beat in X of last Y cards) is persistence across weeks — the only evidence the card trusts with capital. A big edge still marked TOO EARLY has not earned that trust yet.

quiz.q: What does the new 🖨 Save / print button on the report card give you?
a: A clean, dated one-page copy you can save as a PDF to compare week to week
A way to place real trades
A live feed that updates by itself
quiz.why: It opens a self-contained, dated version of the card — deep-dive, every flag, the whole ladder — to print or Save as PDF. Saving one every week or two lets you watch a flag climb or fade over time, which is exactly how a report card is meant to be used.

title: 29 · Anatomy of a card — every number explained
steps: Every line has the same three parts

Read any line — a single flag or a combo — as three layers. Top: the NAME, its Strength /10 score, and a plain verdict (“beat the market” or “did NOT beat”). Middle: the stats — how often it fired and how it did afterwards. Bottom: the reliability line — did the edge last, and has it kept working. Read top-to-bottom, but trust the BOTTOM line the most. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 104' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='12' y='10' width='296' height='26' rx='5' fill='rgba(245,200,76,.08)' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='20' y='27' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>NAME · Strength 7.4/10 · verdict</text><text x='300' y='27' fill='#54627f' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='end' font-family='sans-serif'>layer 1</text><rect x='12' y='40' width='296' height='26' rx='5' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='20' y='57' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>fired 206× · 54% higher · edge +1.87% · median · wins/losses</text><text x='300' y='57' fill='#54627f' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='end' font-family='sans-serif'>layer 2</text><rect x='12' y='70' width='296' height='26' rx='5' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='20' y='87' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>tier · ✓ both halves · tape · track record</text><text x='300' y='87' fill='#54627f' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='end' font-family='sans-serif'>layer 3</text><text x='160' y='12' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='1' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'></text></svg>
“fired 206×” and “54% higher”

“Fired” is the sample size — how many times this flag or combo actually happened across every share in the graded window. More fires means more trustworthy. “54% higher after 5d” means that of those times, 54% of the shares were higher five trading days later — a little better than a coin toss. On its own that means little; it is the edge that counts.
EDGE — the one number that matters

Edge is the honest measure: the average amount those shares beat the TYPICAL share over the next five days. “+1.87%” means they outran the average share by 1.87%. If the whole market rose and they just rode along, the edge is near zero. It strips out lucky good-market weeks so you see the signal’s OWN contribution, not the tide.
The tier badge — how PROVEN, not how big

SOLID, PROMISING and TOO EARLY grade the EVIDENCE, not the size. SOLID = 50+ fires AND statistically strong (unlikely to be luck). PROMISING = 30+ fires AND moderately strong. TOO EARLY = not enough evidence yet. NO EDGE = well-tested but it simply did not work. Watch out: a flag that fired thousands of times can be SOLID on a tiny +0.20% edge — that means “reliably tiny”, not “great”.
Median, wins and losses — the shape

“Median” is the MIDDLE outcome — half did better, half worse — so it shows the typical case, unmoved by one giant winner. If the median sits well below the edge, a few big winners are lifting the average. “wins +8.65% / losses −7.42%” is the payoff shape: the average winning move versus the average losing move.
The durability check: ✓ held up in both halves

The app cuts the window in two and checks the edge in BOTH halves. A green ✓ “held up in both halves” means it showed in both — a durable pattern. A red ✗ “faded in one half” means the edge lived in only one stretch — fragile, and a reason to distrust even a high score. This is the single best durability tell on the card.
The tape: 🟩 risk-on / 🟥 risk-off

“tape” shows how the edge did on days the market was broadly UP (🟩 risk-on) versus broadly DOWN (🟥 risk-off), with the fire count in brackets. A signal that only works on 🟩 days needs a friendly market to help it; one that holds on 🟥 days as well is sturdier. It tells you what MOOD the signal leans on.
📜 the track record — the real test

“beat in 3 of last 3 cards” counts how many of the report cards you have SAVED had this line working. This is the most important mark on the whole card: one good week can be luck, but a signal that keeps beating across many saved cards is the only kind that has earned real capital. Save a card regularly (🖨) so this history builds up.
Two-way flags and their up/down splits

🔷 Block day and 🥇 Vol record fire on BOTH up-days and down-days, so they do not show one pooled score — they say “↓ scored up/down” and split into 🟢 price-up and 🔴 price-down just below, each with its own /10. Always judge the split you would actually trade, never the combined flag: the pooled number can look SOLID while both real halves are weak.
🧩 Combinations — does agreement help?

A combo is two or three flags firing on the SAME share, the SAME day. “each flag alone (edge)” shows what each leg is worth by itself — and the combo is often far stronger than either. In one real example two flags worth −0.00% and +0.08% alone were worth +1.04% TOGETHER. Agreement between weak signals can create an edge neither has alone — that is the whole point of this section.
The habit that ties it together — read right-to-left

Do not start at the score. Start at the 📜 track record and the ✓ both-halves tick — durability first — then the tier badge, THEN the edge and the /10. A 5.5 that has held across three cards is worth more than an 8.9 that just appeared. Proven-and-modest beats big-and-unproven, every single time. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 92' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='160' y='14' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>read every line RIGHT to LEFT - durability before size</text><rect x='244' y='26' width='68' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='278' y='40' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>track record</text><text x='278' y='50' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>+ both halves</text><line x1='240' y1='41' x2='224' y2='41' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='218,37 226,41 218,45' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='156' y='26' width='64' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='188' y='40' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>tier badge</text><text x='188' y='50' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>how proven</text><line x1='152' y1='41' x2='136' y2='41' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='130,37 138,41 130,45' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='72' y='26' width='60' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='102' y='40' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>edge</text><text x='102' y='50' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>how big</text><line x1='68' y1='41' x2='52' y2='41' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='46,37 54,41 46,45' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='8' y='26' width='40' height='30' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='28' y='40' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>/10</text><text x='28' y='50' fill='#54627f' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>last</text><text x='160' y='80' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the score is the SUMMARY - the evidence sits at the right end</text></svg>

quiz.q: A combo shows a big edge (+1.9%) and a high score, but the reliability line says ✗ faded in one half. How much should you trust it?
a: Less than the score suggests — the edge only showed in half the window, so it may not be durable
quiz.why: “Faded in one half” means the edge lived in only one stretch of the window. Durability — both halves plus the 📜 track record — matters more than a single big number.

quiz.q: 🔷 Block day shows SOLID with a +0.20% edge over 8,835 fires. Is that a strong signal to trade?
a: No — SOLID just means it is reliably measured; +0.20% is tiny, and its tradeable up/down splits both score low
quiz.why: A huge number of fires makes even a tiny edge statistically “SOLID”. SOLID means reliably measured, not big. Two-way flags must be judged on their up/down splits, which here are both weak.

quiz.q: Which is the single best sign a signal has earned real trust?
a: 📜 “beat in X of last N cards” — persistence across many saved cards
quiz.why: One good card can be luck. A signal that keeps beating across many saved cards over weeks is the only kind with real, forward-looking evidence behind it.

title: 30 · One row, read out loud — a worked example
steps: The row we're going to read

This lesson takes ONE real combo row from a day's report card — 🚀 Breakout + 🏦 Big money? + 🥇 Vol record — and reads every number on it out loud, in plain English. Your card today will show different numbers; that's fine. The numbers change daily — the WAY of reading them is what you're learning here.
Three clues on the same day

The row's name means three clues fired on the SAME share, the SAME day: the price broke above its old high (🚀), the buying volume looked like big money at work (🏦), and it was the share's busiest trading day in ages (🥇). Think of a detective holding three clues at once and asking: together, do they actually mean something? <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='14' width='84' height='28' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='52' y='26' fill='#4ade80' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>price broke</text><text x='52' y='37' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>its old high</text><rect x='10' y='48' width='84' height='28' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='52' y='60' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>big-money-size</text><text x='52' y='71' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>buying</text><rect x='118' y='30' width='84' height='28' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='160' y='42' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>record</text><text x='160' y='53' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>volume</text><line x1='94' y1='28' x2='116' y2='38' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='110,34 118,38 110,42' fill='#8fa0c9'/><line x1='94' y1='62' x2='116' y2='52' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='110,48 118,52 110,56' fill='#8fa0c9'/><line x1='202' y1='44' x2='226' y2='44' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='220,40 228,44 220,48' fill='#8fa0c9'/><rect x='230' y='28' width='82' height='32' rx='6' fill='rgba(248,113,113,.08)' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='271' y='42' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>ONE share,</text><text x='271' y='53' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>ONE day</text><text x='160' y='90' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>three clues agreeing at once - that is what the combo row counts</text></svg>

First, honesty about the ingredients: each clue BY ITSELF barely beat the average share — tiny slivers. That's the whole point of the combo row. The question it answers is whether TOGETHER beats ALONE — and here the three together earned +0.88%, several times any single leg. Agreement mattered.
“fired 32×” — count the experiments

Fired 32 times means this exact three-clue day has happened 32 times across every share in the graded window. Read it as 32 EXPERIMENTS. It is the most important context on the row, because every other number is only as trustworthy as the number of experiments behind it.
“56% higher” — barely better than a coin

Five trading days later, the share was higher 56 times out of 100. A coin gives you 50. So the pattern wins only a little more OFTEN than chance — which is why the next number matters more: how BIG the moves were, not just how many went up.
“edge +0.88%” — the honest extra

Edge is the app's cleanest number: on average these shares did 0.88% BETTER than the typical share over the same five days. If the whole market rose and they just floated up with it, edge would be near zero — it only counts the extra. Beside it, “median +0.90%” says the middle case looks like the average case: no single giant winner is carrying the result.
“wins +8.97% / losses −12.79%” — the sting in the tail

When this combo was right, it made about +9%. When it was wrong, it lost about −12.8%. Read that carefully: it wins a bit more often than it loses, but each loss hurts MORE than each win helps. A pattern can be 'usually right' and still bite. Check this shape on every row you like — it's where nasty surprises hide. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='160' y='14' fill='#f87171' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the sting in the tail</text><rect x='70' y='30' width='34' height='28' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><text x='87' y='76' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>right: +8.97%</text><rect x='190' y='58' width='34' height='40' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><text x='207' y='76' fill='#f87171' font-size='1' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'></text><text x='207' y='44' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>wrong: −12.79%</text><line x1='40' y1='58' x2='280' y2='58' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1'/><text x='160' y='92' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>it wins a bit more often - but bites HARDER when wrong</text></svg>
“TOO EARLY” — promising is not proven

The badge grades EVIDENCE, not size. 32 experiments is short of the ~50-plus the app wants before it will call anything SOLID — like a batsman who's scored well in three games: promising, but you wouldn't pick him for Australia yet. TOO EARLY says exactly that: keep watching, don't lean on it.
“✓ both halves” and the tape counts

Two durability checks. ✓ held up in both halves: the app split history into the older half and the newer half, and the edge showed in BOTH — not a one-season wonder. Then the tape: 🟩 −2.63% (8) / 🟥 +2.05% (24). Most of its fires (24) came on market-down days and that's where it won; it flopped on market-up days — but with only 8 green-day examples, that could easily be noise. Rule: when a bracket count is small, read it as 'too few to conclude', never as a fact.
Why only 1.5/10, when the edge looks fine?

Because the score follows PROOF first, promise second. A TOO EARLY row is capped low no matter how pretty its edge — the app refuses to get excited off 32 experiments. If the pattern keeps firing and keeps working, its tier rises and the score climbs on its own. Proven-and-modest always outranks flashy-and-new.
Say the whole row back in one breath

“Three clues together, 32 tries, wins a little more often than a coin, edge under 1%, bites harder when wrong than it pays when right, durable so far, mostly a red-day pattern — unproven. Watch it; don't lean on it.” THAT is the reading level to aim at for every row on the card — and it's exactly why the 🤖 auto-pilot's strict gate only trades SOLID-tier lines.

quiz.q: A combo shows edge +0.88% but wears TOO EARLY and scores 1.5/10. Why is the score so low?
a: The score grades evidence first — 32 fires isn't proof yet
quiz.why: The /10 follows PROOF. A TOO EARLY line is capped low until ~50+ fires keep working — promise alone never earns a high score.

quiz.q: “wins +8.97% / losses −12.79%” tells you…
a: It wins more often, so it's safe
Each loss hurts more than each win helps — the shape bites
Losses can't happen if you're patient
quiz.why: A pattern can be right more often than wrong and still be dangerous when the average loss is bigger than the average win.

quiz.q: The best way to read “fired 32×” is…
a: 32 experiments — the sample size behind every other number on the row
quiz.why: Fired = how many times the pattern actually happened. Every other number is only as trustworthy as this count.

quiz.q: The tape shows 🟩 −2.63% (8) / 🟥 +2.05% (24). The wise reading of the (8)?
a: Green days are cursed for this combo
Only 8 green-day examples — far too few to conclude anything
It will always lose on green days
quiz.why: Small bracket counts mean noise. Note it, wait for more examples — never treat 8 experiments as a law.

title: 31 · Which line is best? A 10/10, read out loud
steps: Your eye jumps to the biggest score — good

A report card is a leaderboard, and your eye goes straight to the biggest /10. That instinct is RIGHT — but only once you know what the score is built from. This lesson reads a real top line out loud — 🚀 Breakout + 🥇 Vol record, 10/10 on a 10-day card. Your card's numbers will differ; the WAY of reading them is the lesson.
The grade mixes SIZE and PROOF

Picture two kids at school. One aced a single quiz — could be luck. The other got good marks on 133 quizzes, in term one AND term two. Who do you trust? The /10 works like that: a line only reaches the top when its boost is BIG and it has been tested enough times, and kept working, to rule out luck. Lesson 30 showed the bottom of that law — a pretty edge capped at 1.5/10 by TOO EARLY. This is the top of it. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='14' y='16' width='130' height='64' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='79' y='32' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>kid one</text><text x='79' y='48' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>aced ONE quiz</text><text x='79' y='62' fill='#f87171' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>…could be luck</text><rect x='176' y='16' width='130' height='64' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='241' y='32' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>kid two</text><text x='241' y='48' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>good marks on 133</text><text x='241' y='62' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>quizzes, all year</text><text x='160' y='92' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the grade mixes SIZE with PROOF - repetition is the proof</text></svg>
The winning day, in plain English

🚀 Breakout + 🥇 Vol record means one share, one day, two clues at once: the price broke above its old high AND more shares changed hands than on any day in its recorded history. Two different witnesses telling the same story — someone wants in, badly.
“each flag alone: +1.07% / +0.92%” — together +3.62%

Honesty about the ingredients first. Breakout alone beat the market by about +1.07%; Vol record alone +0.92%. Added up, that's about +2 — but the combo earned +3.62%. TOGETHER carried more information than the sum of the parts. Agreement is the signal.
“fired 133× · SOLID” — enough experiments

133 experiments clears the ~50-plus bar the app demands before it will call anything proven, and the edge kept showing up — that's the SOLID badge, and it's the ONLY way a line is allowed near the top scores. Same law as lesson 30, opposite ending: proof first, promise second.
“52% higher · wins +16.81% / losses −12.05%”

Ten trading days later, only 52 in 100 were higher — barely better than a coin! The money is in the SIZE, not the frequency: when right it averaged +16.81%, when wrong −12.05%. Like a coin that barely favours heads, but heads pays $17 while tails costs $12. Plenty of good patterns look exactly like this — which means you must EXPECT losers, nearly half the time.
“median +0.38%” — stay humble

The MIDDLE share barely moved. The team score is carried by star performers, the way one great batsman can carry an innings. So never read 10/10 as 'every one of these flies'. Read it as 'the group clearly beat the market on average — thanks to some big winners'. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='14' y='57' width='15' height='3' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='37' y='56' width='15' height='4' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='60' y='58' width='15' height='2' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='83' y='55' width='15' height='5' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='106' y='57' width='15' height='3' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='129' y='56' width='15' height='4' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='152' y='58' width='15' height='2' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='175' y='57' width='15' height='3' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='198' y='56' width='15' height='4' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='221' y='57' width='15' height='3' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='244' y='16' width='15' height='44' rx='1.5' fill='#f5c84c'/><line x1='10' y1='60' x2='300' y2='60' stroke='#3a4a7a' stroke-width='1'/><text x='130' y='76' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>most fires: barely moved (median +0.38%)</text><text x='258' y='20' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the stars</text><text x='258' y='32' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>carry it</text><text x='160' y='94' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>52% higher is coin-flip odds - the money is in the SIZE of the wins</text></svg>
Durability: ✓ both halves, and the tape twins

✓ held up in both halves: the edge showed in the older half of history AND the newer half — not a one-season wonder. Tape: 🟩 +3.64% (39) / 🟥 +3.61% (94) — it worked on market-up days AND market-down days, almost identically. Twin tape readings are rare and are exactly the durability a top score wants. (Lesson 30's bracket rule still applies: 39 green-day examples is decent, not enormous.)
Why it beat the 9/10 and 8.2/10 below it

The runners-up were no slouches: ⤴ MA cross + 🔷 Block day actually rose MORE OFTEN (57%, edge +1.96%), and 🚀 Breakout + 🔷 Block day fired far more (775×, edge +1.18%). But the grade weighs size-of-boost and weight-of-proof TOGETHER, and +3.62% on SOLID evidence is the strongest well-proven claim on the card. 'Best' means best at THIS question — biggest proven boost — not most frequent, and not most often up.
Best THIS period — rare, and not a buy button

Two warnings before you fall in love. This is last term's report: ~140 days, graded on that card's outcome window (this one was the 10d research view — the 🤖 auto-pilot still grades on the 5-day card). And it's RARE: 133 fires across ~1,400 shares in seven months is roughly one appearance per trading day somewhere in the whole market — you wait for it; you can't order one. A strong combo is a lead to keep watching across weekly cards — the 📜 track record, persistence across weeks, is the only evidence that deserves capital.

quiz.q: Line A: edge +3.62%, 133 fires, SOLID. Line B: edge +5.00%, 12 fires, TOO EARLY. Which scores higher?
a: B — the bigger edge always wins
A — the score follows proof first, and 12 fires isn't evidence yet
quiz.why: The /10 grades EVIDENCE before size. A flashy edge off 12 experiments stays capped low; 133 experiments that kept working earn the top.

quiz.q: The 10/10 line was higher only 52% of the time — barely a coin. Where did its edge come from?
a: It secretly rose far more often than shown
Size, not frequency: wins averaged +16.81% vs losses −12.05%
quiz.why: Barely-better-than-a-coin can still be a great pattern when the ups are much bigger than the downs. Expect losers — nearly half the time.

quiz.q: Each flag alone: +1.07% and +0.92%. Together: +3.62%. The right conclusion?
a: Stacking any two flags always multiplies the edge
These two clues agreeing carried more information than either alone
One of the flags must be broken
quiz.why: Two witnesses, same story — agreement was the signal HERE. But every combo must prove itself; some combos add nothing.

quiz.q: So a 10/10 on today's card means…
a: The best-PROVEN boost of THIS period — a lead to keep watching across weekly cards
The 🤖 bot will buy it tomorrow
quiz.why: One good period proves nothing about the future. Persistence across 📜 cards is the real test — and the bot's own strict gate still reads the 5-day card.

title: 32 · Why the counts don't add up (and which ones must)
steps: A puzzle from a real card

🔷 Block day: fired 6,626×. Its 🟢 price-up line: 4,289. Its 🔴 price-down line: 4,162. But 4,289 + 4,162 = 8,451 — MORE than the parent's 6,626?! A sharp reader spotted this and asked if the card was broken. It isn't — and understanding why teaches you how every count on the card is made. (Your numbers will differ; the mechanics are the lesson.)
The repeat-blocker

To keep the stats honest, once a line fires on a share, that SAME line ignores that share for the next 10 trading days (or 5, or 30 — the card's outcome window). Why? Because a share having a week-long volume storm would otherwise be counted five times while its outcomes all overlap — the same price move graded again and again. One fire, one clean experiment, no double-marking.
Three lines, three clocks

Here's the key: 'Block day', 'Block day on a price-up day' and 'Block day on a price-down day' are THREE SEPARATE LINES on the card — and each runs its OWN repeat-blocker clock. The parent line asks 'did a block day happen?'. The splits ask different questions: 'did a block day happen on a rising day?' and '…on a falling day?'. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' separate clocks</text><rect x='10' y='20' width='94' height='52' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='57' y='34' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='700' up + down counts can legitimately EXCEED the parent’s</text></svg>
Watch the clocks disagree

Day 1: block day, price up → the parent counts it (its clock starts), the up-line counts it. Day 4: block day, price DOWN → the parent's clock says 'counted you 3 days ago — blocked', but the down-line has never fired on this share, so IT counts it. Parent total: 1. Splits total: 2. Multiply that little story across ~1,400 shares and 140 days and you get 6,626 versus 8,451.
Proof, from the same card

Compare 🥇 Vol record: parent 469, splits 244 + 216 = 460 — nearly equal! New all-time volume records are RARE; they almost never cluster inside 10 days, so the three clocks barely disagree. Block day is the most COMMON flag on the card (any day with volume over double its 90-day average), so it clusters constantly and the clocks disagree a lot. The gap between parent and splits is literally a measure of how much a flag bunches up.
The split that MUST add up

Now the opposite check. Block day's tape split read 🟩 1,910 / 🟥 4,716 — and 1,910 + 4,716 = 6,626, the parent's count EXACTLY. Why does this one balance? Because the tape split divides the parent line's own counted fires — every counted fire happened on either a market-up day or a market-down day, one bucket each. If THAT sum ever missed, it would be a real bug. Same on every line: tape brackets add up; up/down sibling lines don't have to. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0'
