y='74' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>a tape split shares the parent’s clock, so it sums EXACTLY</text><text x='160' y='87' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>up/down splits run their own clocks, so they may not - both are correct</text></svg>
Why not share one clock?

Imagine the splits borrowed the parent's clock. A down-day block firing 3 days after an up-day block would never reach the down-line at all — the split stats would be biased toward whichever direction happened to fire FIRST. Separate clocks keep each line's own evidence clean. The price of that honesty: counts across different lines can never be added together.
Longer windows widen the gap

On a 5-day card the blocker lasts 5 days; on a 10-day card, 10. Twice the blocking means more clustered repeats get swallowed by the parent's clock while the splits still catch theirs — so switching the outcome window to 10d or 30d makes the parent-vs-splits gap BIGGER. Not a bug either; the same mechanics, stretched.
The rule to keep

Every line on the card answers ITS OWN question, with its own no-repeat rule, and its stats are clean for that question. So: compare a line WITH ITSELF across weeks (the 📜 track record), and use tape brackets as the only counts that must balance. Never grade a line by whether its count matches some other line's — they were never counting the same thing.

quiz.q: Block day fired 6,626× but its up-split + down-split = 8,451. What's going on?
a: Each line runs its own no-repeat clock, so clustered fires land differently across the three lines
quiz.why: Parent and splits are separate lines with separate 10-day blockers. When block days bunch up inside the window, the parent's single clock swallows repeats the splits' two clocks still catch.

quiz.q: Which numbers MUST add up to the parent's count, exactly?
a: No numbers on a card ever add up
quiz.why: The tape split divides the parent's own counted fires — each one lands in exactly one bucket. That sum failing would be a genuine bug; sibling lines summing differently is by design.

quiz.q: Why does each line get its own repeat-blocker clock?
a: To make the counts look bigger
Sharing one clock would bias the splits toward whichever direction happened to fire first
quiz.why: A down-block 3 days after an up-block would never reach the down-line under a shared clock. Separate clocks keep each line's evidence clean — at the cost of counts that can't be summed across lines.

quiz.q: Switching the card from 5d to 10d makes the parent-vs-splits gap…
a: Widen — the blocker window doubled, so more clustered repeats are swallowed
quiz.why: Longer outcome windows mean longer blocking. Common, clustering flags like Block day diverge more; rare flags like Vol record barely move.

title: 33 · The 🎯 Watch Score — how a share earns its /10 today
steps: Two different /10s — don't mix them up

The app has TWO ten-point scores, and they answer different questions. The 📋 report card's /10 grades a PATTERN — thousands of history experiments, proof plus edge. The 🎯 Watch Score grades ONE SHARE, TODAY — 'how strong does its current setup look right now?' One judges the recipe; the other judges tonight's ingredients. This lesson is the second one. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 92' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='14' width='146' height='60' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#60a5fa' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='83' y='30' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>report card /10</text><text x='83' y='46' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>grades a PATTERN over</text><text x='83' y='58' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>thousands of past fires</text><rect x='164' y='14' width='146' height='60' rx='6' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='237' y='30' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>Watch Score /10</text><text x='237' y='46' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>grades ONE share’s</text><text x='237' y='58' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>setup TODAY</text><text x='160' y='88' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>two different /10s answering two different questions - never mix them</text></svg>
The question it asks

'Is someone quietly collecting this share right now?' Big buyers try not to be noticed — they buy patiently, day after day, which leaves fingerprints in the price and volume. The Watch Score adds up four of those fingerprints into a pot of 10 points. Every point is explainable — nothing hidden.
Ingredient 1 — Accumulation days (the backbone, max 7)

Look at the last 10 trading days. A day only ticks if it passes BOTH boxes: ☑ closed HIGHER than the day before, AND ☑ volume at least 1.5× its normal (measured against the months before). Each ticked day earns +0.7, up to 7 points. Price nudging up while far more shares than usual change hands is the classic sign of quiet collecting — which is why this ingredient is deliberately the biggest by far.
Ingredient 2 — Price streak (max 1.5)
How many up-days IN A ROW, ending today? +0.4 per day, capped at 1.5. Steady climbing beats one jumpy day — three modest green days say more than one wild one.
Ingredient 3 — Volume streak (max 1)
How many days in a row of above-average volume? +0.3 per day, capped at 1. Interest that keeps showing up, rather than one flash of attention.
Ingredient 4 — Today's kick (max 0.5)

A little extra if today itself was green: today's rise ÷ 10, capped at 0.5 (so up 3% adds 0.3). This is DELIBERATELY the smallest ingredient — one exciting day can never fake a good score. Slow, quiet, repeated buying outranks a single pop, always.
Add it up — a worked share

Four things are added together, and they are deliberately not weighted equally. Accumulation — how many recent days closed up on heavy volume — carries more than the other three put together. A price streak adds a little. A volume streak adds a little less. Today’s move adds least of all, on purpose. So a share with steady, unremarkable accumulation scores well, and a share that jumped this morning on one day’s volume does not. Tick any share and press Rate selected to see its own working, line by line. The bands read: 7–10 STRONG (green), 4–6.9 BUILDING (gold), 2–3.9 EARLY, under 2 MINIMAL. Our share is 'Building' — real signs of collecting, not yet the full picture.
Where the bot uses it

In 📋 My trading rules the 'Min Watch Score' box is a gate: the 🤖 bot only considers shares from its chosen source lane scoring AT OR ABOVE it. Set 4 = Building or better (a wider net). All three presets — 🛡 Defender, ⚖ All-rounder and ⚡ Hunter — use 7 = Strong only: choosier, fewer buys. And you can see any share's live breakdown yourself: tick it, press Rate selected, and the points are listed line by line ('accumulation days, price streak, volume streak, today’s move').
What it does NOT say

The Watch Score reads TODAY'S setup only. It knows nothing about proof and promises nothing about tomorrow — a share can score 9 tonight and fall anyway. Its job is to FIND candidates; the 📋 report card's proof-first /10 decides which SIGNALS on those candidates deserve trust. The bot demands both: a share above your gate AND flags the card has actually graded well. Find-it-today, trust-it-because-of-history — and practice money while you learn.

quiz.q: What's the difference between the Watch Score and the report card's /10?
a: They're the same number in two places
Watch Score rates ONE share's setup today; the card's /10 rates a PATTERN across history
The Watch Score predicts the future, the card doesn't
quiz.why: Watch Score = tonight's ingredients on one share. Report card = proof about a recipe, from thousands of past experiments. The bot needs both.

quiz.q: An accumulation day only ticks when…
a: The share closed higher, on volume at least 1.5× its normal — BOTH boxes
Any day the share went up
Any day the volume was big
quiz.why: It's the combination that matters: price nudging up WHILE far more shares than usual change hands is the fingerprint of quiet collecting. Either alone doesn't tick.

quiz.q: Why is 'today's kick' capped at just 0.5 of the 10 points?
a: So one exciting day can't fake a good score — slow repeated buying must outrank a single pop
quiz.why: The score is built so the patient pattern (up to 7 points across 10 days) dwarfs any single day's excitement (max 0.5).

quiz.q: Setting the bot's Min Watch Score to 7 means…
a: The bot buys anything scoring above 4
Only Strong setups are even considered — choosier, fewer buys
quiz.why: It's a candidate gate, nothing more. 7+ = Strong band only (the 🏆 best-practice choice); no score guarantees anything about tomorrow.

title: 34 · Edge — where every point comes from
steps: The card's cleanest number

Edge is the most important number on the report card: the honest EXTRA a pattern earned over the market — not 'did it go up', but 'did it beat the typical share'. This lesson builds it from scratch using one real row: 🚀 Breakout + ⤴ MA cross, fired 31×, edge +4.03% on a 10-day card. Your numbers will differ; the recipe never does.
One fire = one experiment

Each time the combo fired, the app pretend-buys at the NEXT day's closing price — never the flag day's own close, because a flag only exists once the market has shut. You can't buy a price that's already gone; the measurement refuses hindsight the same way you'd have to. It then holds for the card's outcome window (5, 10 or 30 trading days) and measures the move.
The ±35% seatbelt

Any single outcome is capped at ±35%. One freak share that triples (or collapses) can never hijack a whole row's story — it still counts, just with its seatbelt on. Long windows would truncate more without this; it keeps rows comparable. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='24' y='54' width='20' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><rect x='60' y='48' width='20' height='16' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><rect x='96' y='56' width='20' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><rect x='132' y='50' width='20' height='14' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><rect x='168' y='20' width='20' height='44' rx='1.5' fill='#f5c84c'/><line x1='150' y1='6' x2='196' y2='6' stroke='#54627f' stroke-width='0'/><rect x='204' y='20' width='20' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><line x1='16' y1='20' x2='300' y2='20' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><text x='20' y='14' fill='#f87171' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>the ±35% seatbelt</text><text x='236' y='34' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>a freak tripler is</text><text x='236' y='44' fill='#f87171' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>clipped at the line</text><text x='160' y='86' fill='#54627f' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>one wild outlier can never hijack a whole row’s story</text></svg>
The yardstick — same dates, every share

Now the clever part. Every one of the ~1,400 graded shares gets the IDENTICAL measurement over the IDENTICAL dates. Their average answers one question: 'what did the TYPICAL share do, entered that same day?' That average is the yardstick each fire is measured against.
Subtract — one fire's edge points

One fire's edge = its own move MINUS the typical share's move over the same dates. Say the fire's share made +6.0% while the typical share made +1.97% — that fire contributes +4.03 edge points (illustrative numbers). Market ripped and the share just floated with it? Edge ≈ 0. Market crashed and the share fell LESS? Edge is positive. Only the extra ever counts. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 96' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='46' y='24' width='30' height='36' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><text x='61' y='74' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>the fire’s share</text><text x='61' y='86' fill='#4ade80' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>+6.0%</text><text x='120' y='46' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='15' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>−</text><rect x='150' y='48' width='30' height='12' rx='1.5' fill='#8fa0c9'/><text x='165' y='74' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='7.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>typical share,</text><text x='165' y='86' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>same dates: +1.97%</text><text x='224' y='46' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='15' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>=</text><rect x='252' y='36' width='30' height='24' rx='1.5' fill='#f5c84c'/><text x='267' y='74' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='7.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>edge points</text><text x='267' y='86' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>+4.03%</text><text x='160' y='14' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>one fire’s edge = its move minus the market’s, same dates</text></svg>
Average the gaps — that's the row

31 fires → 31 gaps → their average is the row's edge: +4.03%. Nothing else goes in. And the losers are IN that average — this row lost on nearly half its fires (wins +14.62% / losses −13.91%); the edge survives because the ups outweighed the downs, not because losses were hidden.
Two families of numbers on every row

RAW numbers — '55% higher', median, wins/losses — are the moves before any subtraction: what holding actually felt like. MARKET-ADJUSTED numbers — the edge, and the tape split (🟩 +3.08% (11) / 🟥 +4.55% (20) on this row) — have the market's same-date result already removed. The tape split is simply the edge recomputed twice: once for fires that started on market-up days, once for market-down days.
Why the subtraction is per-day

Because it makes every era honest. A flag that fired mostly during a boom would look brilliant measured raw — the boom did the work. Subtracting each fire's own start-date market result strips that out, so rows from different weeks, months and moods can sit on the same card and be compared fairly.
Edge says how BIG — the tier says how SURE

This very row carried a fat +4.03% yet wore PROMISING with '✗ faded in one half': only 31 experiments, and the edge lived mostly in one era. Edge measures size; the tier (fires + consistency) measures certainty; the /10 follows proof first. That's why the 🤖 auto-pilot's gate only ever leans on SOLID lines — and why a big edge on a young line means 'watch closely', never 'bet big'.

quiz.q: Why does the measurement buy at the NEXT day's close instead of the flag day's close?
a: A flag only exists after the close — buying that same close would be hindsight you could never repeat
quiz.why: The app measures only what a real person could actually do: see the flag after the close, act the next day. No hindsight, no flattery.

quiz.q: A fire's share made +2.0%; the typical share made +2.0% over the same dates. Its edge points?
a: 0 — only the extra over the market counts
quiz.why: Edge subtracts the same-date market result. Floating up with the tide earns nothing; beating the tide is the only thing that scores.

quiz.q: What's the difference between edge and numbers like '55% higher' or wins/losses?
a: Edge has the market's same-date result subtracted; the others are raw moves
Edge is always the bigger number
quiz.why: Raw numbers describe the ride. Edge is the market-adjusted extra — the only number where a boom can't do the work for the flag.

quiz.q: A row shows edge +4.03% but only 31 fires and '✗ faded in one half'. The right read?
a: Bet big — the edge is huge
Edge says how big, the tier says how sure — an unproven line stays on watch
quiz.why: Size and certainty are different questions. 31 one-era experiments is promise, not proof — which is why the /10 caps it and the bot only trades SOLID.

title: 35 · Field guide I — the bullish flags, drawn
steps: A field guide, not a recipe book

Each flag is a picture-story: what the day LOOKS like and why it might matter. Deliberately no tuned trigger numbers here — the exact recipes stay locked in the engine (that's your protection as a customer too: an edge everyone can copy stops being an edge). What you need is to RECOGNISE the stories — and let the 📋 report card tell you which ones have actually been earning their keep. (Your numbers and settings may differ — the mechanics are the lesson.)
🚀 Breakout — the ceiling gives way

Every old high is a ceiling where sellers once won. A breakout is the day price pushes THROUGH that ceiling on convincing volume — the crowd that kept winning there just lost. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='8' y1='34' x2='312' y2='34' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><text x='10' y='28' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='9' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>old high — the ceiling</text><polyline points='10,72 40,64 70,68 100,58 130,62 160,52 190,56 220,44 250,38 275,30 305,16' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><circle cx='275' cy='30' r='3.5' fill='#4ade80'/><text x='240' y='14' fill='#4ade80' font-size='10' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>🚀 break</text><rect x='12' y='79' width='9' height='7' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='33' y='77' width='9' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='54' y='80' width='9' height='6' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='75' y='78' width='9' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='96' y='79' width='9' height='7' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='117' y='76' width='9' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='138' y='78' width='9' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='159' y='77' width='9' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='180' y='79' width='9' height='7' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='201' y='78' width='9' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='222' y='77' width='9' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='243' y='76' width='9' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='264' y='64' width='9' height='22' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><rect x='285' y='60' width='9' height='26' rx='1.5' fill='#4ade80'/><text x='10' y='97' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>volume: ordinary…</text><text x='252' y='97' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>…then heavy</text></svg>The volume matters as much as the price: a break on thin volume is a whisper that often fades; on heavy volume it's a statement.
🕵️ Informed? — someone seems to know

The sneakiest story on the card: price only NUDGES up — nothing exciting — but far more shares than usual quietly change hands. That mismatch is the classic fingerprint of informed money building a position slowly, trying not to move the price. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='10,58 60,56 110,57 160,53 210,54 260,50 305,47' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2'/><text x='190' y='40' fill='#4ade80' font-size='9' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>price: a quiet nudge up</text><rect x='16' y='80' width='11' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='42' y='78' width='11' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='68' y='81' width='11' height='7' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='94' y='79' width='11' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='120' y='80' width='11' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='146' y='78' width='11' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='172' y='79' width='11' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='198' y='80' width='11' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='224' y='79' width='11' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='250' y='46' width='11' height='42' rx='1.5' fill='#f5c84c'/><text x='238' y='38' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='9' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'></text><text x='252' y='60' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='13' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>🕵️</text><text x='10' y='99' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>volume: ordinary days…</text><text x='238' y='99' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>…one shouts</text></svg>Price whispers, volume shouts.
🏦 Big money? — institution-sized buying

An up day whose volume is the size only institutions usually produce. Funds can't buy small — when they act, the footprint is heavy. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='10,66 70,60 130,62 190,50 250,40 305,26' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><rect x='16' y='79' width='13' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='46' y='77' width='13' height='11' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='76' y='80' width='13' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='106' y='78' width='13' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='136' y='79' width='13' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='166' y='78' width='13' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='196' y='42' width='13' height='46' rx='1.5' fill='#60a5fa'/><rect x='226' y='50' width='13' height='38' rx='1.5' fill='#60a5fa'/><text x='196' y='16' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>🏦 big-money-size days</text><text x='10' y='99' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>an up move powered by unusually large buying</text></svg>One 🏦 day is interesting; several near each other start looking like a program of buying.
⤴ MA cross — the tide turns

Average the last 20 days of prices and the last 50. When the fast (20-day) line climbs above the slow (50-day) line, the RECENT trend has overtaken the long one — momentum has genuinely shifted, not just bounced. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='10,44 60,46 110,49 160,52 210,54 260,57 305,59' fill='none' stroke='#8fa0c9' stroke-width='2'/><text x='262' y='70' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>50-day (slow)</text><polyline points='10,74 55,72 100,68 145,62 190,55 235,48 280,40 305,35' fill='none' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.2'/><text x='150' y='88' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>20-day (fast)</text><circle cx='224' cy='52' r='4' fill='none' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='2'/><text x='196' y='32' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='10' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>⤴ the cross</text></svg>It fires rarely per share (the lines only cross so often), which is part of its charm.
🧑‍💼 DIR✓ — insiders bought with their own money

Not a price pattern at all: a confirmed director filing from the last 5 days, straight from official announcements. Directors know their company. It appears in the Signals column as its own badge and the bot can require it as a co-signal.
Reading them together

One flag = one witness. The report card's 🧩 combos exist because two witnesses telling the SAME story on the SAME day (🚀+🥇, 🕵️+🏦…) have historically carried more information than either alone — lesson 31 showed a pair worth more than the sum of its parts. But which pairs deserve trust changes over time, which is exactly what your 📋 card re-measures every day.

quiz.q: Why does a breakout care about volume, not just the new high?
a: A break on heavy volume is a statement; on thin volume it's a whisper that often fades
quiz.why: The ceiling breaking matters most when real money did the breaking.

quiz.q: 🕵️ Informed? looks for…
a: A huge price jump on huge volume
A quiet price nudge on unusually heavy volume — someone building a position without moving the price
quiz.why: The MISMATCH is the story: volume shouting while price whispers is how careful, possibly informed, buyers behave.

quiz.q: Why aren't the exact trigger numbers printed in this lesson?
a: The recipes stay in the engine — an edge everyone can copy stops being an edge; the card proves which stories work without exposing how they're computed
quiz.why: Meaning public, recipe private — you get the understanding AND the protection.

title: 36 · Field guide II — two-way flags, warnings & sequences
steps: Some flags face both ways

🥇 Vol record and 🔷 Block day describe EVENTS — unusual activity — not directions. The same event on a rising day and a falling day means opposite things, which is why the report card scores them BOTH ways (the ↓ scored up/down rows from lesson 32). (Your numbers and settings may differ — the mechanics are the lesson.)
🥇 Vol record — the busiest day ever

More shares traded than on ANY day in the share's recorded history. Someone was urgent. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='12' y='72' width='10' height='12' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='36' y='66' width='10' height='18' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='60' y='74' width='10' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='84' y='68' width='10' height='16' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='108' y='71' width='10' height='13' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='132' y='62' width='10' height='22' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='156' y='69' width='10' height='15' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='180' y='65' width='10' height='19' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='204' y='70' width='10' height='14' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='228' y='67' width='10' height='17' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='252' y='69' width='10' height='15' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='276' y='26' width='10' height='58' rx='1.5' fill='#f5c84c'/><line x1='8' y1='26' x2='312' y2='26' stroke='#3a4a7a' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><text x='10' y='20' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>old volume record</text><text x='232' y='20' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='9.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>🥇 NEW record</text><text x='10' y='98' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>price UP that day → accumulation story · price DOWN → alarm bell</text></svg>Price up that day → urgency to GET IN (accumulation). Price down → urgency to GET OUT (alarm). The card's split rows tell you which version has been predictive lately.
🔷 Block day — big parcels on the move

Volume beyond double a normal day — the size that suggests large holders repositioning rather than retail trickle. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='14' y='70' width='13' height='14' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='44' y='67' width='13' height='17' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='74' y='72' width='13' height='12' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='104' y='68' width='13' height='16' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='134' y='71' width='13' height='13' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='164' y='69' width='13' height='15' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='194' y='70' width='13' height='14' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='224' y='40' width='13' height='44' rx='1.5' fill='#60a5fa'/><rect x='254' y='44' width='13' height='40' rx='1.5' fill='#60a5fa'/><line x1='8' y1='52' x2='312' y2='52' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4'/><text x='10' y='47' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>double a normal day</text><text x='232' y='30' fill='#60a5fa' font-size='10' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>🔷 blocks</text><text x='10' y='98' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>big parcels changing hands — someone repositioning</text></svg>The most common flag on the card (busy days happen a lot), so it leans on combos and the up/down split for its meaning.
📉 Quiet selling? — the exit footprint (traders: distribution)

The mirror of 🕵️ Informed?: price drifting DOWN while volume swells. Somebody large is leaving without wanting a fuss. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 100' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polyline points='10,30 60,36 110,34 160,44 210,50 260,60 305,68' fill='none' stroke='#f87171' stroke-width='2.2'/><rect x='16' y='79' width='13' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='46' y='78' width='13' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='76' y='80' width='13' height='8' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='106' y='77' width='13' height='11' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='136' y='79' width='13' height='9' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='166' y='78' width='13' height='10' rx='1.5' fill='#54627f'/><rect x='196' y='48' width='13' height='40' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><rect x='226' y='52' width='13' height='36' rx='1.5' fill='#f87171'/><text x='200' y='26' fill='#f87171' font-size='9' font-weight='700' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>📉 heavy selling days</text><text x='10' y='99' fill='#8fa0c9' font-size='8' font-weight='400' text-anchor='start' font-family='sans-serif'>price drifting DOWN while volume swells — quiet exiting</text></svg>On the card it's graded as a WARNING — 'working' means the shares it flagged went on to LAG the market. A warning that predicts falls is doing its job; it is never a buy signal.
Sequences — accumulation, then ignition

A different question from same-day combos: quiet-buying flags (🕵️ 🏦 🥇 🔷) in the 1–3 days BEFORE, then an ignition flag (🚀 or ⤴) today. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 84' style='max-width:340px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='14' y1='42' x2='306' y2='42' stroke='#3a4a7a' stroke-width='2'/><circle cx='50' cy='42' r='9' fill='#0d1530' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.6'/><text x='50' y='46' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='10' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>🕵️</text><circle cx='105' cy='42' r='9' fill='#0d1530' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.6'/><text x='105' y='46' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='10' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>🏦</text><circle cx='160' cy='42' r='9' fill='#0d1530' stroke='#f5c84c' stroke-width='1.6'/><text x='160' y='46' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='10' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>🥇</text><circle cx='250' cy='42' r='13' fill='#0d1530' stroke='#4ade80' stroke-width='2.4'/><text x='250' y='47' fill='#4ade80' font-size='12' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>🚀</text><text x='105' y='70' fill='#f5c84c' font-size='8.5' font-weight='400' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>quiet buying — the 1–3 days before</text><text x='250' y='72' fill='#4ade80' font-size='8.5' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' font-family='sans-serif'>ignition — today</text><polygon points='300,42 290,37 290,47' fill='#4ade80'/></svg>Fuel first, spark second — the classic pattern of a position built quietly and then revealed. The card's 🔀 sequence rows grade exactly this.
Warnings score in their own direction

On the ladder, a warning line earns a HIGH score when its flagged shares genuinely underperformed — high score = reliable warning, and it stays tagged '· warning' so it can never be mistaken for a buy. Direction-aware honesty, everywhere.

quiz.q: A 🥇 Vol record fired on a DOWN day. The story is…
a: Urgency to get OUT — the alarm-bell version; check the card's price-down row for whether it's been predictive
quiz.why: Two-way flags take their meaning from the day's direction — that's why the card splits and scores them both ways.

quiz.q: 📉 Quiet selling? is 'working' when its shares…
a: LAG the market afterwards — it's a warning, and predicting falls is its job
quiz.why: Warnings are graded in their own direction. A reliable warning scores high and still is never a buy.

quiz.q: A sequence row like 🥇 (prior 3d) → 🚀 is asking…
a: Did two flags fire the same day?
Did quiet buying in the days before lead to ignition today — fuel, then spark?
Did the share pay a dividend?
quiz.why: Sequences test the accumulation-then-move story across days; same-day combos test agreement within one day.

title: 37 · The bot's funnel — 3,500 shares to a handful of buys
steps: One picture of the whole machine

Every data day, the 🤖 bot pours the whole market in the top and lets the gates say no. What survives at the bottom becomes a PRACTICE buy — logged, priced at the next open, brokerage charged. <svg viewBox='0 0 320 284' style='max-width:360px;width:100%;display:block;margin:8px 0'
